verses.1:1: And these are the names of the sons of Israel who came into Egypt with Jacob; each man and his household came:
verses.1:4: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
verses.1:5: And all the persons who came out of Jacob's loins were seventy persons, while Joseph was already in Egypt.
verses.1:6: And Joseph died, along with all his brothers and all of that generation.
verses.1:7: Yet the sons of Israel were fruitful and teemed, and they multiplied and grew immensely mighty, so that the land became filled with them.
verses.1:8: Then a new king rose over Egypt, one who did not know Joseph.
verses.1:9: And he said to his people, "Look, the people of the sons of Israel are more numerous and mightier than we are.
verses.1:10: Come, let us act shrewdly toward them, or else they will multiply, and should war occur, they too will join those who hate us, fight against us, and go up from the land."
verses.1:11: So they placed overseers of forced labor over them in order to afflict them with their burdens; and they built storage cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Rameses.
verses.1:12: Yet the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and the more they spread; and they felt dread because of the sons of Israel.
verses.1:13: And the Egyptians forced the sons of Israel to labor with brutality.
verses.1:14: They made their lives bitter with severe labor, with mortar and bricks and with every kind of labor in the field—all their labor that they exacted from them with brutality.
verses.1:15: Then the king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah and the name of the second was Puah.
verses.1:16: And he said, "When you assist the Hebrew women in childbirth and look upon the birthstool, if it is a son, put him to death; and if it is a daughter, let her live."
verses.1:17: Yet the midwives feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had spoken to them; instead, they kept the boys alive.
verses.1:18: So the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and said to them, "Why have you done this thing and kept the boys alive?"
verses.1:19: And the midwives said to Pharaoh, "Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women; for they are vigorous—before the midwife comes to them, they have given birth."
verses.1:20: And God did good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew very mighty.
verses.1:21: And because the midwives feared God, He made households for them.
verses.1:22: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, "Every son who is born, you shall throw into the Nile, yet every daughter you shall keep alive."
verses.2:1: And a man from the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi.
verses.2:2: And the woman conceived and gave birth to a son; and she saw that he was good, so she hid him for three months.
verses.2:3: And when she could no longer hide him, she took a basket of papyrus for him and coated it with bitumen and pitch; she placed the child in it and placed it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.
verses.2:4: And his sister stationed herself at a distance to learn what would be done to him.
verses.2:5: Then Pharaoh's daughter went down to bathe at the Nile, while her young women were walking alongside the Nile; and she saw the basket in the midst of the reeds, and sent her maidservant, who took it.
verses.2:6: She opened it and saw the child, and look, a boy was crying; and she felt compassion for him and said, "This is one of the children of the Hebrews."
verses.2:7: Then his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter, "Should I go and call for you a nursing woman from the Hebrew women, so she can nurse the child for you?"
verses.2:8: Pharaoh's daughter told her, "Go." So the young woman went and called the mother of the child.
verses.2:9: Then Pharaoh's daughter said to her, "Take this child with you and nurse him for me, and I myself will pay your wages." So the woman took the child and nursed him.
verses.2:10: And the child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became a son to her. And she called his name Moses, and she said, "Because I drew him from the water."
verses.2:11: And it happened in those days, after Moses had grown up, that he went out to his brothers and looked upon their burdens; and he saw an Egyptian man striking a Hebrew man from among his brothers.
verses.2:12: So he turned this way and that, and when he saw that no one was there, he struck the Egyptian down and hid him in the sand.
verses.2:13: He went out on the second day, and look, two Hebrew men were fighting together; and he said to the wrongdoer, "Why are you striking your neighbor?"
verses.2:14: And he replied, "Who set you as a ruler and a judge over us? Do you intend to kill me just as you killed the Egyptian?" So Moses was afraid and said, "Indeed, the matter is known."
verses.2:15: When Pharaoh heard about this matter, he sought to kill Moses; yet Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian, and he sat down by the well.
verses.2:16: And the priest of Midian had seven daughters; they came, drew water, and filled the troughs in order to water the flock of their father.
verses.2:17: Yet the shepherds came and drove them off; so Moses rose up and saved them, and he watered their flock.
verses.2:18: And they came to their father Reuel, and he said, "Why have you come so quickly today?"
verses.2:19: And they replied, "An Egyptian man rescued us from the hand of the shepherds; moreover, he actually drew water for us and watered the flock."
verses.2:20: And he said to his daughters, "And where is he? Why then did you leave the man? Call for him so that he may eat bread."
verses.2:21: And Moses consented to live with the man, and he gave Zipporah his daughter to Moses.
verses.2:22: And she gave birth to a son, and he called his name Gershom, because he said, "I have become a sojourner in a foreign land."
verses.2:23: And it happened during those many days that the king of Egypt died; and the sons of Israel groaned because of the servitude and cried out, and their cry for help went up to God from the servitude.
verses.2:24: So God heard their moaning, and God remembered His covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
verses.2:25: And God saw the sons of Israel, and God knew.
verses.3:1: Now Moses was tending the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian; and he led the flock beyond the wilderness and came to the mountain of God, to Horeb.
verses.3:2: And the angel of the LORD appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of a bush; he looked, and see—the bush was burning with fire, yet the bush was not being consumed.
verses.3:3: Then Moses said, "Let me turn aside now and see this great sight, why the bush does not burn up."
verses.3:4: And the LORD saw that he had turned aside to see, so God called out to him from within the bush and said, "Moses, Moses!" And he answered, "Here I am."
verses.3:5: And He said, "Do not approach here; slip off your sandals from your feet, because the place where you are standing is holy ground."
verses.3:6: And He said, "I am the God of your father—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." So Moses concealed his face, because he was afraid to gaze at God.
verses.3:7: And the LORD said, "I have indeed seen the affliction of My people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their outcry because of their taskmasters; for I know their pains.
verses.3:8: And I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land to a good and wide land, to a land flowing with milk and honey, to the place of the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Hivites and the Jebusites.
verses.3:9: And now, look, the outcry of the sons of Israel has come to Me, and I have also seen the oppression by which the Egyptians are oppressing them.
verses.3:10: And now, come, that I may send you to Pharaoh; and bring out My people, the sons of Israel, from Egypt."
verses.3:11: And Moses said to God, "Who am I, that I would go to Pharaoh and that I would bring out the sons of Israel from Egypt?"
verses.3:12: And He said, "Indeed, I will be with you, and this is the sign for you that I Myself have sent you: when you bring the people out from Egypt, you will serve God on this mountain."
verses.3:13: And Moses said to God, "Look, I am going to the sons of Israel and will say to them, 'The God of your fathers has sent me to you,' and they will say to me, 'What is His name?' What am I to say to them?"
verses.3:14: And God said to Moses, "I WILL BE WHO I WILL BE." And He said, "This is what you shall say to the sons of Israel: 'I WILL BE has sent me to you.'"
verses.3:15: And God said further to Moses, "This is what you shall say to the sons of Israel: 'The LORD, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.' This is My name forever, and this is My memorial from generation to generation.
verses.3:16: Go and gather the elders of Israel and say to them, 'The LORD, the God of your fathers, has appeared to me—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—saying, "I have indeed attended to you and to what has been done to you in Egypt,
verses.3:17: and I have said that I will bring you up from the affliction of Egypt into the land of the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Hivites and the Jebusites, into a land flowing with milk and honey."'
verses.3:18: And they will heed your voice; then you and the elders of Israel shall come to the king of Egypt and say to him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met us; and now, please let us go a journey of three days into the wilderness, so that we may offer sacrifice to the LORD our God.'
verses.3:19: Yet I Myself know that the king of Egypt will not permit you to go, not even by a strong hand.
verses.3:20: So I will extend My hand and strike Egypt with all My wonders that I will perform in its midst; and after that he will send you out.
verses.3:21: And I will give favor to this people in the eyes of the Egyptians; and it will happen that when you go, you will not go empty-handed.
verses.3:22: Instead, each woman shall ask her neighbor and the woman lodging in her house for objects of silver and objects of gold, and garments; and you shall put them on your sons and on your daughters, and so you will plunder the Egyptians."
verses.4:1: Moses answered and said, "But look, they will not believe me and they will not listen to my voice, for they will say, 'The LORD did not appear to you.'"
verses.4:2: Then the LORD said to him, "What is this in your hand?" He said, "A staff."
verses.4:3: He said, "Throw it to the ground." So he threw it to the ground, and it became a snake, and Moses fled from before it.
verses.4:4: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Reach out your hand and seize it by its tail"—so he reached out his hand and took firm hold of it, and it became a staff in his palm—
verses.4:5: "in order that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, appeared to you."
verses.4:6: Then the LORD said to him again, "Please put your hand into your bosom." He put his hand into his bosom, and he drew it out, and look, his hand was leprous, like snow.
verses.4:7: Then He said, "Put your hand back into your bosom." So he put his hand back into his bosom, and he drew it out from his bosom, and look, it was restored like his flesh.
verses.4:8: "And it will happen, if they do not believe you and do not listen to the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the latter sign.
verses.4:9: And it will happen, if they do not believe even these two signs and do not listen to your voice, that you shall take some of the water of the Nile and pour it out onto the dry ground; and the water that you take from the Nile will become blood on the dry ground."
verses.4:10: Then Moses said to the LORD, "Please, Lord, I am not a man of words, neither yesterday nor the day before, nor since You have spoken to Your servant, for I am heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue."
verses.4:11: The LORD said to him, "Who made a mouth for mankind, or who makes one mute or deaf, or seeing or blind? Is it not I, the LORD?
verses.4:12: So now, go, and I Myself will be with your mouth and will instruct you in what you are to speak."
verses.4:13: But he said, "Please, Lord, send now by the hand of whomever You will send."
verses.4:14: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Moses, and He said, "Is there not Aaron your brother, the Levite? I know that he indeed speaks well. Moreover, look, he is coming out to meet you, and he will see you and rejoice in his heart.
verses.4:15: You shall speak to him and place the words in his mouth; and I Myself will be with your mouth and with his mouth, and I will instruct you in what you shall do.
verses.4:16: He himself will speak for you to the people; and it will be that he will serve as a mouth for you, and you will serve as God to him.
verses.4:17: And this staff you shall take in your hand, with which you will perform the signs."
verses.4:18: So Moses went and returned to Jether his father-in-law, and he said to him, "Please let me go and return to my brothers who are in Egypt and see whether they are still alive." And Jethro said to Moses, "Go in peace."
verses.4:19: And the LORD said to Moses in Midian, "Go, return to Egypt, for all the men who were seeking your life have died."
verses.4:20: Moses took his wife and his sons, mounted them on a donkey, and returned to the land of Egypt; and Moses took the staff of God in his hand.
verses.4:21: The LORD said to Moses, "When you go to return to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders that I have placed in your hand; yet I Myself will harden his heart, and he will not let the people go.
verses.4:22: Then you shall say to Pharaoh, 'This is what the LORD says: My son, My firstborn, is Israel.
verses.4:23: And I said to you, "Let My son go so that he may serve Me," yet you refused to let him go. Look, I am about to kill your son, your firstborn.'"
verses.4:24: Now it happened on the way, at the lodging place, that the LORD met him and sought to put him to death.
verses.4:25: Then Zipporah took a flint and cut off the foreskin of her son, and she touched it to his feet and said, "Indeed, a bridegroom of blood you are to me!"
verses.4:26: So He let go of him. Then she said, "A bridegroom of blood," because of the circumcision.
verses.4:27: And the LORD said to Aaron, "Go into the wilderness to meet Moses." He went, met him at the mountain of God, and kissed him.
verses.4:28: And Moses reported to Aaron all the words of the LORD with which He had sent him, and all the signs that He had commanded him to perform.
verses.4:29: So Moses and Aaron went and gathered all the elders of the sons of Israel.
verses.4:30: And Aaron spoke all the words that the LORD had spoken to Moses, and he performed the signs before the eyes of the people.
verses.4:31: Then the people believed; and they heard that the LORD had visited the sons of Israel and that He had seen their affliction, so they bowed down and worshiped.
verses.5:1: And afterward Moses and Aaron came in and said to Pharaoh, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Let My people go, so that they may celebrate a festival for Me in the wilderness."
verses.5:2: And Pharaoh said, "Who is the LORD, that I should listen to His voice to let Israel go? I do not know the LORD, and furthermore, I will not let Israel go."
verses.5:3: So they said, "The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please let us go a journey of three days into the wilderness and sacrifice to the LORD our God, or else He may strike us with pestilence or with the sword."
verses.5:4: And the king of Egypt said to them, "Why, Moses and Aaron, are you pulling the people away from their tasks? Go to your burdens!"
verses.5:5: Pharaoh also said, "Look, the people of the land are numerous now, and you are making them rest from their burdens!"
verses.5:6: So on that day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters over the people and their foremen, saying,
verses.5:7: "You shall no longer give straw to the people for making bricks as before; they themselves shall go and gather straw for themselves.
verses.5:8: Yet the quota of bricks that they were making before, you shall impose on them; you shall not reduce it. For they are idle; therefore they are crying out, saying, 'Let us go, let us sacrifice to our God.'
verses.5:9: Let the labor weigh heavy on the men, that they may work at it and pay no attention to words of falsehood."
verses.5:10: Then the taskmasters of the people and their foremen went out and spoke to the people, saying, "This is what Pharaoh says: I am not giving you straw.
verses.5:11: Go yourselves, get straw for yourselves from wherever you find it, for not a thing will be reduced from your labor."
verses.5:12: Then the people spread out across all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
verses.5:13: And the taskmasters were pressing hard, saying, "Complete your tasks, each day's quota in its day, just as when there was straw."
verses.5:14: And the foremen of the sons of Israel, whom Pharaoh's taskmasters had appointed over them, were beaten and asked, "Why have you not completed your prescribed share in making bricks as before, either yesterday or today?"
verses.5:15: So the foremen of the sons of Israel came and cried out to Pharaoh, saying, "Why do you do this to your servants?
verses.5:16: No straw is given to your servants, yet they say to us, 'Make bricks!' And look, your servants are being beaten, yet your own people are at fault."
verses.5:17: But he said, "Idle, you are idle! Therefore you are saying, 'Let us go, let us sacrifice to the LORD.'
verses.5:18: Now then, go, work! Straw will not be given to you, yet you shall deliver the tally of bricks."
verses.5:19: And the foremen of the sons of Israel saw themselves in trouble when they were told, "You shall not reduce your bricks, each day's quota in its day."
verses.5:20: Then they encountered Moses and Aaron, who were standing to meet them as they came out from Pharaoh.
verses.5:21: And they said to them, "May the LORD look upon you and judge, because you have made our scent stink in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to kill us."
verses.5:22: So Moses returned to the LORD and said, "Lord, why have You caused harm to this people? Why is it that You sent me?
verses.5:23: From the time I came to Pharaoh to speak in Your name, he has caused harm to this people, and You have not rescued Your people at all."
verses.6:1: And the LORD said to Moses, "Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh, because by a strong hand he will release them, and by a strong hand he will drive them from his land."
verses.6:2: And God spoke to Moses and said to him, "I am the LORD.
verses.6:3: And I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty, yet as for My name, the LORD, I was not known to them.
verses.6:4: Moreover, I established My covenant with them to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings, in which they sojourned.
verses.6:5: And I Myself have also heard the groaning of the sons of Israel, whom the Egyptians are forcing into servitude, and I have remembered My covenant.
verses.6:6: Therefore say to the sons of Israel, 'I am the LORD, and I will bring you out from beneath the burdens of Egypt, and I will rescue you from their servitude, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with great judgments.
verses.6:7: And I will take you for Myself as a people, and I will be God to you; then you will know that I am the LORD your God, the One who brings you out from beneath the burdens of Egypt.
verses.6:8: And I will bring you into the land that I lifted My hand to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, and I will give it to you as a possession. I am the LORD.'"
verses.6:9: So Moses spoke in this way to the sons of Israel, but they did not listen to Moses because of shortness of spirit and because of harsh servitude.
verses.6:10: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.6:11: "Go in, speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, so that he will release the sons of Israel from his land."
verses.6:12: But Moses spoke before the LORD, saying, "Look, the sons of Israel have not listened to me; how then will Pharaoh listen to me, when I am uncircumcised of lips?"
verses.6:13: Then the LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, and He commanded them concerning the sons of Israel and concerning Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to bring the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
verses.6:14: These are the heads of their fathers' houses: the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, were Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi; these are the clans of Reuben.
verses.6:15: And the sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of the Canaanite woman; these are the clans of Simeon.
verses.6:16: And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari; and the years of Levi's life were one hundred thirty-seven years.
verses.6:17: The sons of Gershon were Libni and Shimei, according to their clans.
verses.6:18: And the sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel; and the years of Kohath's life were one hundred thirty-three years.
verses.6:19: And the sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites according to their generations.
verses.6:20: And Amram took Jochebed, his aunt, for himself as a wife, and she bore Aaron and Moses to him; and the years of Amram's life were one hundred thirty-seven years.
verses.6:21: And the sons of Izhar were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
verses.6:22: And the sons of Uzziel were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
verses.6:23: And Aaron took Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon, for himself as a wife, and she bore to him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
verses.6:24: And the sons of Korah were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph; these are the clans of the Korahites.
verses.6:25: And Eleazar, the son of Aaron, took one of the daughters of Putiel for himself as a wife, and she bore Phinehas to him. These are the heads of the fathers of the Levites according to their clans.
verses.6:26: This is the Aaron and Moses to whom the LORD said, "Bring the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt according to their divisions."
verses.6:27: They were the ones who spoke to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to bring the sons of Israel out of Egypt; this was Moses and Aaron.
verses.6:28: Now it came about on the day the LORD spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
verses.6:29: that the LORD spoke to Moses, saying, "I am the LORD; speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, all that I am speaking to you."
verses.6:30: But Moses said before the LORD, "Look, I am uncircumcised of lips, so how will Pharaoh listen to me?"
verses.7:1: Then the LORD said to Moses, "See, I have appointed you as God to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother will be your prophet.
verses.7:2: You will speak all that I command you, and Aaron your brother will speak to Pharaoh so that he should release the sons of Israel from his land.
verses.7:3: But I Myself will harden Pharaoh's heart, and I will multiply My signs and My wonders in the land of Egypt.
verses.7:4: And Pharaoh will not listen to you, so I will set My hand against Egypt and bring My divisions, My people the sons of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.
verses.7:5: And the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I stretch out My hand over Egypt and bring the sons of Israel out from among them."
verses.7:6: Then Moses and Aaron acted; exactly as the LORD had commanded them, so they did.
verses.7:7: Now Moses was eighty years old and Aaron was eighty-three years old at the time they spoke to Pharaoh.
verses.7:8: Then the LORD said to Moses and to Aaron,
verses.7:9: "When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, 'Produce a wonder for yourselves,' then you will say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh,' and it will become a serpent."
verses.7:10: So Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and they did so, just as the LORD had commanded; and Aaron threw his staff down before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.
verses.7:11: Then Pharaoh too summoned the wise men and the sorcerers; and they too, the magicians of Egypt, did the same through their secret arts.
verses.7:12: Each man threw his staff down, and they became serpents; yet Aaron's staff swallowed up their staffs.
verses.7:13: Yet Pharaoh's heart grew hard, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken.
verses.7:14: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Pharaoh's heart is unyielding; he has refused to release the people.
verses.7:15: Go to Pharaoh in the morning; look, he is going out to the water. Station yourself to meet him on the bank of the Nile, and take in your hand the staff that was turned into a snake,
verses.7:16: and say to him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying: Release My people so that they may serve Me in the wilderness. Yet look, up to now you have not listened.
verses.7:17: This is what the LORD says: By this you will know that I am the LORD. Look, I am about to strike the water that is in the Nile with the staff that is in My hand, and it will be turned into blood.
verses.7:18: The fish that are in the Nile will die, and the Nile will stink, and the Egyptians will weary themselves trying to drink water from the Nile.'"
verses.7:19: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their canals, over their ponds, and over every collection of their waters, so that they become blood,' and there will be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in wood and in stone."
verses.7:20: So Moses and Aaron did so, just as the LORD had commanded; and he lifted up the staff and struck the water that was in the Nile before the eyes of Pharaoh and before the eyes of his servants, and all the water that was in the Nile was turned into blood.
verses.7:21: And the fish that were in the Nile died, and the Nile stank, so that the Egyptians could not drink water from the Nile; and the blood was throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.7:22: Yet the magicians of Egypt did the same through their secret arts; so Pharaoh's heart grew hard, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken.
verses.7:23: Then Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not set his heart even on this.
verses.7:24: Then all the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink, because they were unable to drink from the waters of the Nile.
verses.7:25: And seven days were completed after the LORD struck the Nile.
verses.7:26: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh and say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Release My people so that they may serve Me.
verses.7:27: But if you are unwilling to release them, look, I am about to plague all your territory with frogs.
verses.7:28: And the Nile will teem with frogs; they will come up and go into your house, into your bedroom, and onto your bed, into the houses of your servants and among your people, and into your ovens and into your kneading troughs.
verses.7:29: And upon you, and upon your people, and upon all your servants the frogs will come up.'"
verses.8:1: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, over the canals, and over the pools, and bring up the frogs over the land of Egypt.'"
verses.8:2: So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
verses.8:3: Yet the magicians did the same with their secret arts, and they brought up frogs over the land of Egypt.
verses.8:4: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Plead with the LORD so that He may remove the frogs from me and from my people, and I will send the people away so that they may sacrifice to the LORD."
verses.8:5: And Moses said to Pharaoh, "Take the honor over me: for what time shall I plead for you, for your servants, and for your people, to cut off the frogs from you and from your houses? Only in the Nile will they remain."
verses.8:6: And he said, "For tomorrow." And he said, "According to your word, so that you may know that there is no one like the LORD our God.
verses.8:7: The frogs will depart from you, from your houses, from your servants, and from your people; only in the Nile will they remain."
verses.8:8: Then Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried out to the LORD concerning the frogs that He had imposed upon Pharaoh.
verses.8:9: And the LORD did according to the word of Moses, and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courtyards, and out of the fields.
verses.8:10: They piled them up in heaps upon heaps, and the land stank.
verses.8:11: When Pharaoh saw that there was relief, he made his heart heavy and did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken.
verses.8:12: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the ground, and it will become gnats throughout all the land of Egypt.'"
verses.8:13: And they did so: Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the ground, and the gnats came upon people and upon animals; all the dust of the ground became gnats throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.8:14: The magicians did likewise with their secret arts to bring out the gnats, yet they were not able; and the gnats were on people and on animals.
verses.8:15: Then the magicians said to Pharaoh, "It is the finger of God." Yet Pharaoh's heart grew hard, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken.
verses.8:16: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Rise early in the morning and station yourself before Pharaoh—look, he is going out to the water—and say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Send My people away so that they may serve Me.
verses.8:17: For if you do not send My people away, look, I am sending a swarm of flies against you, against your servants, against your people, and into your houses; and the houses of Egypt will be full of the swarm of flies, and also the ground on which they are.
verses.8:18: Yet on that day I will set apart the land of Goshen, on which My people stand, so that no swarm of flies will be there, in order that you may know that I am the LORD in the midst of the land.
verses.8:19: And I will put redemption between My people and your people; tomorrow this sign will take place.'"
verses.8:20: And the LORD did so: a heavy swarm of flies came into Pharaoh's house and the houses of his servants, and throughout all the land of Egypt the land was being ruined because of the swarm of flies.
verses.8:21: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Go, sacrifice to your God in the land."
verses.8:22: And Moses said, "It is not right to do so, for we would be sacrificing what is an abomination to the Egyptians to the LORD our God. If we sacrifice what is an abomination to the Egyptians before their eyes, will they not stone us?
verses.8:23: We will go a journey of three days into the wilderness and sacrifice to the LORD our God, just as He tells us."
verses.8:24: And Pharaoh said, "I myself will send you away, and you may sacrifice to the LORD your God in the wilderness; only you must not go very far away. Plead on my behalf."
verses.8:25: And Moses said, "Look, I am going out from you, and I will plead with the LORD so that the swarm of flies will depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people tomorrow; only let Pharaoh not deal deceitfully again by not sending the people away to sacrifice to the LORD."
verses.8:26: So Moses went out from Pharaoh and pleaded with the LORD.
verses.8:27: And the LORD did according to the word of Moses, and the swarm of flies departed from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people; not one remained.
verses.8:28: Yet Pharaoh made his heart heavy this time also, and he did not send the people away.
verses.9:1: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh and speak to him, 'This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: Send My people away so that they may serve Me.
verses.9:2: For if you refuse to send them away and are still keeping hold of them,
verses.9:3: look, the hand of the LORD is coming upon your livestock that are in the field—on the horses, on the donkeys, on the camels, on the herds, and on the flocks—a very heavy pestilence.
verses.9:4: Yet the LORD will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, so that nothing will die of all that belongs to the sons of Israel.'"
verses.9:5: And the LORD set an appointed time, saying, "Tomorrow the LORD will do this thing in the land."
verses.9:6: So the LORD did this thing on the next day, and all the livestock of Egypt died; yet of the livestock of the sons of Israel, not one died.
verses.9:7: And Pharaoh sent, and look, not even one of the livestock of Israel had died. Yet Pharaoh's heart became heavy, and he did not send the people away.
verses.9:8: Then the LORD said to Moses and to Aaron, "Take for yourselves handfuls of soot from a kiln, and let Moses toss it toward the sky in the sight of Pharaoh.
verses.9:9: It will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and it will become boils breaking out into blisters on people and on animals throughout all the land of Egypt."
verses.9:10: So they took soot from the kiln and stood before Pharaoh, and Moses tossed it toward the sky; and it became boils with blisters breaking out on people and on animals.
verses.9:11: And the magicians were not able to stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were on the magicians and on all the Egyptians.
verses.9:12: Yet the LORD made Pharaoh's heart hard, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken to Moses.
verses.9:13: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Rise early in the morning and station yourself before Pharaoh, and say to him, 'This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: Send My people away so that they may serve Me.
verses.9:14: For this time I am sending all My plagues against your heart, and upon your servants and your people, so that you may know that there is no one like Me in all the earth.
verses.9:15: For by now I could have stretched out My hand and struck you and your people with pestilence, and you would have been wiped out from the earth.
verses.9:16: However, for this reason I have kept you standing: in order to show you My power, and so that My name may be recounted throughout all the earth.
verses.9:17: You are still exalting yourself against My people by not sending them away.
verses.9:18: Look, about this time tomorrow I will rain down very heavy hail, such as has never been in Egypt from the day it was founded until now.
verses.9:19: So now, send and bring your livestock to safety, along with everything that belongs to you in the field. Every person and animal that is found in the field and is not gathered into the house—the hail will come down on them, and they will die.'"
verses.9:20: Whoever among Pharaoh's servants feared the word of the LORD made his servants and his livestock flee into the houses;
verses.9:21: but whoever did not set his heart on the word of the LORD left his servants and his livestock in the field.
verses.9:22: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward the sky so that there may be hail throughout all the land of Egypt, on people, on animals, and on every plant of the field in the land of Egypt."
verses.9:23: So Moses stretched out his staff toward the sky, and the LORD sent thunder and hail, and fire ran down to the earth; and the LORD rained hail upon the land of Egypt.
verses.9:24: So there was hail, and fire flaring continuously in the midst of the hail—very heavy, such as had never been in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.
verses.9:25: And the hail struck throughout all the land of Egypt everything that was in the field, from people to animals; and the hail struck every plant of the field and shattered every tree of the field.
verses.9:26: Only in the land of Goshen, where the sons of Israel were, there was no hail.
verses.9:27: Then Pharaoh sent and summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them, "This time I have sinned; the LORD is the righteous One, and I and my people are the wicked.
verses.9:28: Plead with the LORD, for there has been enough of God's thunder and hail; and I will send you away, and you shall stay no longer."
verses.9:29: And Moses said to him, "As soon as I leave the city, I will spread out my palms to the LORD; the thunder will cease and there will be no more hail, in order that you may know that the earth belongs to the LORD.
verses.9:30: Yet as for you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear the LORD God."
verses.9:31: Now the flax and the barley were struck down, for the barley was in the ear and the flax was in bud.
verses.9:32: But the wheat and the emmer were not struck down, for they ripen late.
verses.9:33: So Moses went out from Pharaoh and out of the city, and he spread out his palms to the LORD; and the thunder and the hail ceased, and rain did not pour down to the earth.
verses.9:34: When Pharaoh saw that the rain, the hail, and the thunder had ceased, he sinned again and made his heart heavy, he and his servants.
verses.9:35: So Pharaoh's heart grew hard, and he did not send the sons of Israel away, just as the LORD had spoken by the hand of Moses.
verses.10:1: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh, for I Myself have made his heart heavy and the heart of his servants, so that I may set these signs of Mine in his midst,
verses.10:2: and so that you may recount in the ears of your son and your son's son how I dealt ruthlessly with Egypt, and My signs that I placed among them; and you will know that I am the LORD."
verses.10:3: So Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and said to him, "This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: 'How long do you refuse to humble yourself before Me? Let My people go so that they may serve Me.
verses.10:4: For if you refuse to let My people go, look, tomorrow I am bringing locusts into your territory.
verses.10:5: And they will cover the surface of the land, so that no one will be able to see the land; and they will eat the remainder of what escaped, which was left for you from the hail, and they will eat every tree sprouting for you from the field.
verses.10:6: And your houses will be filled, and the houses of all your servants, and the houses of all Egypt, something that neither your fathers nor your fathers' fathers have seen from the day they came to be on the earth until this day.'" Then he turned and went out from Pharaoh.
verses.10:7: Then Pharaoh's servants said to him, "How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the men go so that they may serve the LORD their God. Do you not yet know that Egypt is ruined?"
verses.10:8: So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, and he said to them, "Go, serve the LORD your God. Who exactly are the ones going?"
verses.10:9: And Moses said, "With our young and with our old we will go; with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds we will go, for we have a feast to the LORD."
verses.10:10: Then he said to them, "So may the LORD be with you, just as I will let you and your little ones go! Look, evil is right before your face.
verses.10:11: Not so! Go now, you men, and serve the LORD, for that is what you are seeking." Then they were driven out from Pharaoh's presence.
verses.10:12: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, so that they may come up over the land of Egypt and eat every plant of the land, everything that the hail left behind."
verses.10:13: So Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and the LORD drove an east wind across the land all that day and all that night. When morning came, the east wind had carried in the locusts.
verses.10:14: And the locusts came up over all the land of Egypt and settled in all the territory of Egypt, extremely dense; before them there had never been locusts like them, and after them there will never be such again.
verses.10:15: They covered the surface of all the land, so that the land grew dark; and they ate every plant of the land and all the fruit of the trees that the hail had left over, so that nothing green was left over on the trees or among the plants of the field in all the land of Egypt.
verses.10:16: Then Pharaoh hurried to summon Moses and Aaron and said, "I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.
verses.10:17: And now, please forgive my sin just this once, and plead with the LORD your God so that He may remove from me only this death."
verses.10:18: So he went out from Pharaoh and pleaded with the LORD.
verses.10:19: And the LORD turned the wind into a very strong west wind, and it lifted up the locusts and drove them into the Sea of Reeds; not a single locust remained in all the territory of Egypt.
verses.10:20: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the sons of Israel go.
verses.10:21: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward the sky, so that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, darkness one can feel."
verses.10:22: So Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and there was dense darkness in all the land of Egypt for three days.
verses.10:23: They did not see one another, nor did anyone rise from his place for three days; but all the sons of Israel had light in their dwellings.
verses.10:24: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and said, "Go, serve the LORD; only let your flocks and your herds be left behind. Even your little ones may go with you."
verses.10:25: But Moses said, "You yourself must also put sacrifices and burnt offerings into our hands, so that we may offer them to the LORD our God.
verses.10:26: And our livestock too must go with us; not a hoof will be left behind, for we will take from them to serve the LORD our God, and we ourselves do not know with what we are to serve the LORD until we arrive there."
verses.10:27: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he was unwilling to let them go.
verses.10:28: Then Pharaoh said to him, "Get away from me! Watch yourself: do not see my face again, for on the day you see my face, you will die!"
verses.10:29: And Moses said, "You have spoken rightly; I will never see your face again."
verses.11:1: Now the LORD said to Moses, "One more plague I will bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt; after that he will let you go from here. When he lets you go completely, he will surely drive you out from here.
verses.11:2: Speak now in the ears of the people, so that each man may ask his neighbor and each woman her neighbor for articles of silver and articles of gold."
verses.11:3: And the LORD gave the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians. Moreover, the man Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the eyes of Pharaoh's servants and in the eyes of the people.
verses.11:4: And Moses said, "This is what the LORD says: 'About midnight I am going out into the midst of Egypt,
verses.11:5: and every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne to the firstborn of the female servant who is behind the millstones, and every firstborn of the animals.
verses.11:6: And there will be a great outcry in all the land of Egypt, the like of which has never happened before, and the like of which will never happen again.
verses.11:7: But against any of the sons of Israel not a dog will sharpen its tongue, from man to animal, so that you may know that the LORD makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel.'
verses.11:8: And all these servants of yours will come down to me and bow down to me, saying, 'Go out, you and all the people who follow at your feet.' And after that I will go out." Then he went out from Pharaoh in burning anger.
verses.11:9: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that My wonders may multiply in the land of Egypt."
verses.11:10: Now Moses and Aaron performed all these wonders before Pharaoh, yet the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the sons of Israel go from his land.
verses.12:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
verses.12:2: "This month is for you the beginning of months; it shall be first for you of the months of the year.
verses.12:3: Speak to the entire congregation of Israel, saying, 'On the tenth of this month, they shall take for themselves, each man a lamb for a household of fathers, a lamb for each household.
verses.12:4: And if the household is too small for a lamb, then he and his neighbor closest to his house shall take one by a reckoning of persons; each man according to what he eats, you shall reckon for the lamb.
verses.12:5: You shall have a lamb without defect, a male one year old; from the sheep or from the goats you may take it.
verses.12:6: And it shall be in your keeping until the fourteenth day of this month, and the entire assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it at twilight.
verses.12:7: And they shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and on the lintel, on the houses where they will eat it.
verses.12:8: And they shall eat the meat on that night; roasted over fire, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs, they shall eat it.
verses.12:9: Do not eat any of it raw or boiled in any way in water, but rather roasted over fire, its head with its legs and with its inner parts.
verses.12:10: You shall not leave any of it until morning; whatever remains of it until morning you shall burn in the fire.
verses.12:11: And this is how you shall eat it: with your waist belted, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you shall eat it in haste. It is a Passover to the LORD.
verses.12:12: And I will pass through the land of Egypt on that night, and I will strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to beast; and on all the gods of Egypt I will carry out judgments. I am the LORD.
verses.12:13: And the blood shall be for you a sign on the houses where you are; I will see the blood and pass over you, and there shall be no destructive plague among you when I strike in the land of Egypt.
verses.12:14: And this day shall be for you a memorial, and you shall celebrate it as a festival to the LORD; throughout your generations, as a perpetual statute, you shall celebrate it.
verses.12:15: For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; indeed, on the first day you shall clear leaven from your houses, for everyone who eats anything leavened from the first day until the seventh day, that person shall be cut off from Israel.
verses.12:16: And on the first day you shall have a sacred assembly, and on the seventh day a sacred assembly; no work of any kind shall be done on them, only what is to be eaten by every person, that alone may be prepared by you.
verses.12:17: And you shall observe the unleavened bread, for on this very day I brought out your hosts from the land of Egypt; and you shall observe this day throughout your generations as a perpetual statute.
verses.12:18: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month in the evening, you shall eat unleavened bread until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening.
verses.12:19: For seven days no leaven shall be found in your houses, for everyone who eats anything leavened, that person shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether a resident alien or a native of the land.
verses.12:20: You shall eat nothing leavened; in all your dwelling places you shall eat unleavened bread.'"
verses.12:21: Then Moses summoned all the elders of Israel and said to them, "Draw out and take for yourselves from the flock according to your clans, and slaughter the Passover.
verses.12:22: And you shall take a bundle of hyssop, dip it into the blood that is in the basin, and touch the lintel and the two doorposts with some of the blood that is in the basin; and none of you shall go out of the doorway of his house until morning.
verses.12:23: For the LORD will pass through to strike Egypt, and when He sees the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts, the LORD will pass over the doorway and will not permit the destroyer to come into your houses to strike.
verses.12:24: And you shall observe this thing as a statute for you and for your children forever.
verses.12:25: And when you enter the land that the LORD will give you, just as He has spoken, you shall observe this service.
verses.12:26: And it shall be, when your children say to you, 'What is this service to you?'
verses.12:27: then you shall say, 'It is a Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when He struck Egypt and rescued our houses.'" Then the people bowed down and worshiped.
verses.12:28: And the sons of Israel went and carried it out; just as the LORD commanded Moses and Aaron, they did so.
verses.12:29: And it happened at midnight that the LORD struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh sitting on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the dungeon, and every firstborn of the livestock.
verses.12:30: And Pharaoh got up during the night, he and all his servants and all Egypt, and there was a great outcry in Egypt, for there was no house in which there was not someone dead.
verses.12:31: And he called Moses and Aaron during the night and said, "Get up, go out from the midst of my people, both you and the sons of Israel, and go, serve the LORD as you spoke.
verses.12:32: Both your flocks and your herds, take them as you have spoken, and go; and bless me as well."
verses.12:33: And Egypt pressed hard on the people to hasten to send them out of the land, for they said, "All of us are dead!"
verses.12:34: So the people carried their dough before it was leavened, with their kneading bowls bundled in their cloaks on their shoulders.
verses.12:35: And the sons of Israel had done according to the word of Moses, and they asked from the Egyptians silver articles and gold articles and garments.
verses.12:36: And the LORD had given the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians, so they granted their request, and they plundered the Egyptians.
verses.12:37: And the sons of Israel set out from Rameses to Succoth, around six hundred thousand men on foot, apart from little ones.
verses.12:38: And a great mixed multitude also went up with them, along with flocks and herds, very abundant livestock.
verses.12:39: And they baked into unleavened cakes the dough that they had brought out from Egypt, for it had not leavened, because they had been driven out from Egypt and could not linger, and they had not even made provisions for themselves.
verses.12:40: And the stay of the sons of Israel, during which they lived in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.
verses.12:41: And it happened at the end of four hundred and thirty years, on that very day, all the hosts of the LORD came out from the land of Egypt.
verses.12:42: It was a night of vigil by the LORD to bring them out from the land of Egypt; this very night belongs to the LORD, a vigil for all the sons of Israel throughout their generations.
verses.12:43: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "This is the statute concerning the Passover: no foreigner may eat of it;
verses.12:44: but every slave of a man who is bought with money, once you have circumcised him, then he may eat of it.
verses.12:45: A temporary resident or a hired worker shall not eat of it.
verses.12:46: In one house it shall be eaten; you shall not bring any of the meat outside the house, and you shall not break a bone of it.
verses.12:47: The entire congregation of Israel shall observe it.
verses.12:48: And if a resident alien resides with you and wishes to observe the Passover to the LORD, every male belonging to him must be circumcised, and then he may draw near to observe it, and he shall be like a native of the land; but no uncircumcised male may eat of it.
verses.12:49: One law shall apply to the native and to the resident alien who resides in your midst."
verses.12:50: And all the sons of Israel carried it out; just as the LORD commanded Moses and Aaron, they did so.
verses.12:51: And it happened on that very day that the LORD brought out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt according to their hosts.
verses.13:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.13:2: "Consecrate to Me every firstborn, whatever opens every womb among the sons of Israel, both of man and of livestock; it is Mine."
verses.13:3: And Moses said to the people, "Remember this day on which you went out of Egypt, from the house of slaves, because by strength of hand the LORD brought you out from here; and leavened bread shall not be eaten.
verses.13:4: Today you are going out, in the month of Abib.
verses.13:5: And it shall come about, when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, which He swore to your fathers to give to you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you shall perform this service in this month.
verses.13:6: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a festival to the LORD.
verses.13:7: Unleavened bread shall be eaten throughout the seven days; no leavened bread shall be seen with you, and no leaven shall be seen with you within all your borders.
verses.13:8: And you shall tell your son on that day, saying, 'It is on account of what the LORD did for me when I went out of Egypt.'
verses.13:9: And it shall serve you as a sign on your hand and as a reminder between your eyes, so that the instruction of the LORD may be in your mouth; for with a strong hand the LORD brought you out of Egypt.
verses.13:10: And you shall keep this statute at its appointed time, year after year.
verses.13:11: And it shall come about, when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, just as He swore to you and to your fathers, and gives it to you,
verses.13:12: that you shall hand over to the LORD all that opens the womb, along with every first young of livestock that belongs to you; the males belong to the LORD.
verses.13:13: As for every first young of a donkey, you shall redeem it with a sheep or goat, and if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck; and you shall redeem every human firstborn among your sons.
verses.13:14: And it shall come about, when your son asks you in time to come, saying, 'What is this?' that you shall say to him, 'By strength of hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, from the house of slaves.
verses.13:15: And it happened, when Pharaoh hardened himself against letting us go, that the LORD killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of man to the firstborn of livestock. Therefore I sacrifice to the LORD all that opens the womb, the males, while every firstborn of my sons I redeem.
verses.13:16: And it shall serve as a sign on your hand and as frontlets between your eyes, because by strength of hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt.'"
verses.13:17: Now it came about, when Pharaoh sent the people out, that God did not lead them by the road of the land of the Philistines, although it was near; for God said, "Otherwise the people might change their minds when they see war and turn back to Egypt."
verses.13:18: So God brought the people around by the road of the wilderness toward the Red Sea; and equipped for battle, the sons of Israel went up from the land of Egypt.
verses.13:19: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, because Joseph had solemnly made the sons of Israel swear, saying, "God will certainly attend to you, and you shall bring up my bones from here with you."
verses.13:20: And they broke camp from Succoth and encamped at Etham, at the edge of the wilderness.
verses.13:21: Now the LORD was going ahead of them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them on the road, and by night in a pillar of fire to shine light for them, so that they could travel day and night.
verses.13:22: The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not withdraw from ahead of the people.
verses.14:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.14:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel that they turn back and encamp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea; before Baal-zephon, directly opposite it, you shall encamp beside the sea.
verses.14:3: And Pharaoh will say about the sons of Israel, 'They are wandering bewildered in the land; the wilderness has closed in on them.'
verses.14:4: And I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and he will pursue after them; then I will win glory over Pharaoh and over all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD." And they did so.
verses.14:5: And it was reported to the king of Egypt that the people had fled; then the heart of Pharaoh and his servants turned against the people, and they said, "What is this that we have done, that we have sent Israel away from serving us?"
verses.14:6: So he harnessed his chariot and took his people with him.
verses.14:7: He took six hundred select chariots and all the chariots of Egypt, with officers over them all.
verses.14:8: And the LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, so that he pursued after the sons of Israel; meanwhile, the sons of Israel were going out with a raised hand.
verses.14:9: The Egyptians pursued after them and overtook them encamped beside the sea—all the chariot horses of Pharaoh, his horsemen, and his army—by Pi-hahiroth, before Baal-zephon.
verses.14:10: And as Pharaoh approached, the sons of Israel lifted up their eyes, and look, the Egyptians were marching after them; and they were greatly afraid, and the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD.
verses.14:11: And they said to Moses, "Was it for lack of any graves in Egypt that you took us to die in the wilderness? What is this that you have done to us, bringing us out of Egypt?
verses.14:12: Is not this the word we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, 'Let us alone so that we may serve the Egyptians'? For it is better for us to serve the Egyptians than for us to die in the wilderness."
verses.14:13: Then Moses said to the people, "Do not be afraid; take your stand and see the salvation of the LORD that He will perform for you today, for the way you have seen the Egyptians today, you will not see them again forever.
verses.14:14: The LORD will fight on your behalf, and you shall remain silent."
verses.14:15: And the LORD said to Moses, "Why do you cry out to Me? Speak to the sons of Israel that they set out.
verses.14:16: And you, raise your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and split it, so that the sons of Israel may go into the midst of the sea on dry ground.
verses.14:17: And as for Me, look, I am about to harden the heart of the Egyptians so that they will go in after them; and I will win glory over Pharaoh and over all his army, over his chariots and over his horsemen.
verses.14:18: Then the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD, when I win glory over Pharaoh, over his chariots and over his horsemen."
verses.14:19: Now the angel of God, who was going ahead of the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them; the pillar of cloud also moved from ahead of them and stood behind them.
verses.14:20: So it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel; and there was the cloud and the darkness, yet it lit up the night, so that the one did not come near the other all night.
verses.14:21: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the LORD pushed the sea back with a fierce east wind all night and made the sea into dry land; and the waters were split.
verses.14:22: So the sons of Israel went into the midst of the sea on dry ground, with the waters as a wall for them on their right and on their left.
verses.14:23: The Egyptians pursued and went in after them—all of Pharaoh's horses, his chariots, and his horsemen—into the midst of the sea.
verses.14:24: And it happened in the morning watch that the LORD looked down toward the camp of Egypt in the pillar of fire and cloud, and threw the camp of Egypt into confusion.
verses.14:25: He removed the wheels of their chariots so that they drove them with difficulty; and the Egyptians said, "Let us flee from before Israel, for the LORD is fighting for them against Egypt!"
verses.14:26: And the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the sea, that the waters may return over the Egyptians, over their chariots, and over their horsemen."
verses.14:27: So Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and at the approach of morning the sea returned to its steady flow while the Egyptians were fleeing to meet it; and the LORD shook the Egyptians into the midst of the sea.
verses.14:28: And the waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen—all of Pharaoh's army that had gone after them into the sea; not a single one among them was left.
verses.14:29: Yet the sons of Israel walked on dry ground in the midst of the sea, with the waters as a wall for them on their right and on their left.
verses.14:30: And on that day the LORD saved Israel out of the hand of Egypt, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead along the shore of the sea.
verses.14:31: And Israel saw the great hand that the LORD exercised against Egypt, and the people feared the LORD, and they trusted in the LORD and in Moses His servant.
verses.15:1: Then Moses and the sons of Israel sang this song to the LORD and spoke, saying, "I will sing to the LORD, for He is surpassingly exalted; horse and its rider He has cast into the sea.
verses.15:2: My strength and song is the LORD, and He has become salvation for me; this is my God, and I will glorify Him, the God of my father, and I will lift Him high.
verses.15:3: The LORD is a man of battle; the LORD is His name.
verses.15:4: The chariots of Pharaoh and his army He has hurled into the sea, and the finest of his officers were sunk in the Sea of Reeds.
verses.15:5: Deeps covered them; they descended into the depths like a stone.
verses.15:6: Your right hand, LORD, is majestic in strength; Your right hand, LORD, crushes the enemy.
verses.15:7: And in the abundance of Your majesty You tear down those who rise against You; You send out Your burning wrath; it devours them like stubble.
verses.15:8: And by the blast of Your nostrils waters were heaped up; flowing streams stood upright like a mound; deeps congealed in the heart of the sea.
verses.15:9: The enemy said, 'I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the plunder; my soul will have its fill of them; I will unsheathe my sword; my hand will dispossess them.'
verses.15:10: You blew with Your breath; the sea covered them; they plunged like lead in mighty waters.
verses.15:11: Who is like You among the gods, LORD? Who is like You, majestic in holiness, awe-inspiring in praises, performing wonders?
verses.15:12: You extended Your right hand; the earth swallowed them.
verses.15:13: In Your loyal love You led the people whom You redeemed; by Your strength You guided them to Your holy dwelling.
verses.15:14: Peoples have heard; they quake; anguish has seized the inhabitants of Philistia.
verses.15:15: Then the chieftains of Edom were terrified; trembling seizes the mighty ones of Moab; all the inhabitants of Canaan melted away.
verses.15:16: Terror and dread will fall upon them; by the greatness of Your arm they will grow still like a stone, until Your people pass over, LORD, until the people whom You have acquired pass over.
verses.15:17: You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance, the place for Your dwelling that You have made, LORD, the sanctuary, Lord, that Your hands established.
verses.15:18: The LORD will reign forever and ever."
verses.15:19: For Pharaoh's horses entered the sea with his chariots and his horsemen, and the LORD turned the waters of the sea back over them, while the sons of Israel walked on dry ground in the middle of the sea.
verses.15:20: Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron's sister, took the tambourine in her hand, and all the women went out behind her with tambourines and dances.
verses.15:21: And Miriam responded to them, "Sing to the LORD, for He is surpassingly exalted; horse and its rider He has cast into the sea."
verses.15:22: Then Moses led Israel onward from the Sea of Reeds, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; they walked three days in the wilderness and found no water.
verses.15:23: And they arrived at Marah, yet they could not drink water from Marah, for it was bitter; therefore its name was called Marah.
verses.15:24: And the people grumbled against Moses, saying, "What are we to drink?"
verses.15:25: And he cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a tree; he threw it into the water, and the water turned sweet. There He set for them a statute and an ordinance, and there He tested them.
verses.15:26: And He said, "If you carefully listen to the voice of the LORD your God, and do what is upright in His eyes, and pay attention to His commandments, and observe all His statutes, none of the diseases that I placed on Egypt will I place on you, for I am the LORD who heals you."
verses.15:27: And they arrived at Elim, and there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees; so they camped there beside the water.
verses.16:1: And they set out from Elim, and the entire congregation of the sons of Israel arrived at the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they went out from the land of Egypt.
verses.16:2: And the entire congregation of the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness.
verses.16:3: And the sons of Israel said to them, "If only we had died by the hand of the LORD in the land of Egypt, when we sat beside the pot of meat, when we ate bread to satisfaction; for you have brought us out into this wilderness to put this entire assembly to death by hunger."
verses.16:4: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Look, I am going to rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather each day's portion on its day, in order that I may test them, whether they will walk in My instruction or not.
verses.16:5: And it shall be on the sixth day that they will prepare what they bring in, and it will be double what they gather day by day."
verses.16:6: Then Moses and Aaron said to all the sons of Israel, "In the evening you will know that the LORD brought you out from the land of Egypt,
verses.16:7: and in the morning you will see the glory of the LORD, because He hears your grumblings against the LORD. As for us, what are we that you grumble against us?"
verses.16:8: And Moses said, "When the LORD gives you meat to eat in the evening and bread in the morning to be satisfied, because the LORD hears your grumblings that you are grumbling against Him—as for us, what are we? Your grumblings are not against us, but against the LORD."
verses.16:9: And Moses said to Aaron, "Say to the entire congregation of the sons of Israel, 'Draw near before the LORD, for He has heard your grumblings.'"
verses.16:10: And as Aaron was speaking to the entire congregation of the sons of Israel, they turned toward the wilderness, and look, the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud.
verses.16:11: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.16:12: "I have heard the grumblings of the sons of Israel. Speak to them, saying, 'At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be satisfied with bread; then you will know that I am the LORD your God.'"
verses.16:13: So it was in the evening that quail came up and covered the camp, and in the morning a layer of dew lay around the camp.
verses.16:14: And when the layer of dew lifted, look, on the surface of the wilderness there was something fine and flaky, as fine as frost on the ground.
verses.16:15: When the sons of Israel saw it, they said one to another, "What is it?" because they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them, "It is the bread that the LORD has given you for food.
verses.16:16: This is the word that the LORD has commanded: 'Gather from it, each one according to what he eats, an omer per head, according to the number of your persons; each of you shall take for those who are in his tent.'"
verses.16:17: And the sons of Israel did so; they gathered, some gathering much and some little.
verses.16:18: And when they measured it by the omer, the one who gathered much had no surplus, and the one who gathered little had no shortage; each one had gathered according to what he ate.
verses.16:19: And Moses said to them, "No one is to leave any of it until morning."
verses.16:20: Yet they did not listen to Moses; some men left part of it until morning, and it teemed with worms and turned foul, and Moses grew angry with them.
verses.16:21: So they gathered it every morning, each one according to what he ate; and whenever the sun grew hot, it melted away.
verses.16:22: And on the sixth day they gathered double the bread, two omers for each person; and all the leaders of the congregation came and reported it to Moses.
verses.16:23: And he said to them, "It is what the LORD has spoken: Tomorrow is a solemn rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. What you will bake, bake, and what you will boil, boil; and set aside all the surplus for yourselves for safekeeping until the morning."
verses.16:24: So they set it aside until the morning, as Moses had commanded, and it did not turn foul, and there were no maggots in it.
verses.16:25: And Moses said, "Eat it today, because today is a Sabbath to the LORD; you will not find it in the field today.
verses.16:26: For six days you are to gather it, but on the seventh day, a Sabbath, there will be none."
verses.16:27: And on the seventh day some from among the people went out to gather, yet they did not find any.
verses.16:28: And the LORD said to Moses, "How long will you refuse to observe My commandments and My instructions?
verses.16:29: See that the LORD has given you the Sabbath; for that reason He is giving you two days' bread on the sixth day. Stay each of you right where he is; no one is to go out from his place on the seventh day."
verses.16:30: And the people rested on the seventh day.
verses.16:31: And the house of Israel called its name manna; it was white like coriander seed, and its taste was like a wafer with honey.
verses.16:32: And Moses said, "This is the word that the LORD has commanded: 'A full omer of it is for safekeeping throughout your generations, in order that they may see the bread that I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out from the land of Egypt.'"
verses.16:33: And Moses said to Aaron, "Take one jar and put a full omer of manna into it, and set it before the LORD for safekeeping throughout your generations."
verses.16:34: Just as the LORD had commanded Moses, so Aaron set it before the testimony for safekeeping.
verses.16:35: And the sons of Israel ate the manna for forty years, until they reached an inhabited land; they ate the manna until they reached the edge of the land of Canaan.
verses.16:36: Now an omer is one-tenth of an ephah.
verses.17:1: Then the entire congregation of the sons of Israel set out from the wilderness of Sin by their stages at the command of the LORD, and they camped at Rephidim; yet there was no water for the people to drink.
verses.17:2: Then the people contended with Moses and said, "Give us water so that we may drink." Moses said to them, "Why are you contending with me? Why are you testing the LORD?"
verses.17:3: But the people thirsted there for water, and the people grumbled against Moses and said, "Why then did you bring us up from Egypt, to put me and my children and my livestock to death with thirst?"
verses.17:4: So Moses cried out to the LORD, saying, "What am I to do with this people? A little longer and they will stone me."
verses.17:5: The LORD said to Moses, "Pass on ahead of the people, and take some of the elders of Israel with you; also take in your hand your staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
verses.17:6: See, I will stand before you there on the rock at Horeb; you shall strike the rock, and water will come out from it, and the people will drink." And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
verses.17:7: And he called the name of the place Massah and Meribah, because of the contention of the sons of Israel and because they tested the LORD, saying, "Is the LORD in our midst, or not?"
verses.17:8: Now Amalek came and fought with Israel at Rephidim.
verses.17:9: And Moses said to Joshua, "Choose men for us, and go out and fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I will take my stand on the top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand."
verses.17:10: So Joshua did just as Moses had said to him, to fight against Amalek; and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
verses.17:11: And it happened that whenever Moses lifted his hand, Israel prevailed; yet whenever he let his hand down, Amalek prevailed.
verses.17:12: Now Moses' hands were heavy, so they took a stone and placed it under him, and he sat on it; and Aaron and Hur supported his hands, one on this side and one on that side. Thus his hands remained steady until the setting of the sun.
verses.17:13: And Joshua overpowered Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
verses.17:14: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write this as a memorial in the book and put it in the ears of Joshua, for I will completely wipe out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens."
verses.17:15: And Moses built an altar and called its name "The LORD is my banner."
verses.17:16: And he said, "For a hand is upon the throne of the LORD; the LORD will be at war against Amalek from generation to generation."
verses.18:1: Now Jethro, priest of Midian, Moses' father-in-law, heard of everything God had done for Moses and for Israel His people, that the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
verses.18:2: So Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses' wife, after she had been sent away,
verses.18:3: along with her two sons; the name of the one was Gershom, for he said, "I have been a sojourner in a foreign land,"
verses.18:4: and the name of the other was Eliezer, "For the God of my father was my help, and He rescued me from the sword of Pharaoh."
verses.18:5: Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came with his sons and his wife to Moses into the wilderness where he was camped, at the mountain of God.
verses.18:6: And he said to Moses, "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you, and your wife and her two sons with her."
verses.18:7: So Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, and he bowed down and kissed him; they asked each other about their well-being, and then they went into the tent.
verses.18:8: Then Moses recounted to his father-in-law all that the LORD had done to Pharaoh and to Egypt on account of Israel, all the hardship that had befallen them along the way, and how the LORD had rescued them.
verses.18:9: And Jethro rejoiced over all the good that the LORD had done for Israel, whom He had rescued from the hand of Egypt.
verses.18:10: And Jethro said, "Blessed be the LORD, who rescued you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of Pharaoh, who rescued the people from under the hand of Egypt.
verses.18:11: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all the gods; indeed, in the very matter in which they acted arrogantly against them."
verses.18:12: Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices for God; and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat bread with Moses' father-in-law before God.
verses.18:13: And on the next day, Moses sat to judge the people, while the people stood around Moses from morning until evening.
verses.18:14: When Moses' father-in-law saw all that he was doing for the people, he said, "What is this thing that you are doing for the people? Why are you sitting alone while all the people stand around you from morning until evening?"
verses.18:15: Moses said to his father-in-law, "Because the people come to me to inquire of God.
verses.18:16: Whenever a matter arises for them, it comes to me, and I judge between a man and his neighbor, and I make known the statutes of God and His instructions."
verses.18:17: Moses' father-in-law said to him, "The thing you are doing is not good.
verses.18:18: You will surely wear out, both you and this people who are with you, for the matter is too heavy for you; you cannot do it by yourself.
verses.18:19: Now listen to my voice; I will advise you, and may God be with you. You act on behalf of the people before God, and you bring the matters to God.
verses.18:20: And you shall teach them the statutes and the instructions, and make known to them the way in which they should walk and the work that they should do.
verses.18:21: Moreover, you shall look out from all the people capable men who fear God, men of truth who hate dishonest gain, and appoint them over the people as officials of thousands, officials of hundreds, officials of fifties, and officials of tens.
verses.18:22: They shall judge the people at all times; every major matter they shall bring to you, while every minor matter they themselves shall judge. So make it lighter for yourself, and let them bear it with you.
verses.18:23: If you do this thing, and God commands you so, then you will be able to endure, and all this people too will go to their place in peace."
verses.18:24: Then Moses heeded the voice of his father-in-law and did everything that he had said.
verses.18:25: Moses chose capable men from all Israel and appointed them as heads over the people: officials of thousands, officials of hundreds, officials of fifties, and officials of tens.
verses.18:26: And they judged the people at all times; the difficult matter they would bring to Moses, while every minor matter they themselves would judge.
verses.18:27: Then Moses sent his father-in-law off, and he went his way to his own land.
verses.19:1: In the third month after the sons of Israel had gone out from the land of Egypt, on that very day they came into the wilderness of Sinai.
verses.19:2: They set out from Rephidim, came into the wilderness of Sinai, and camped in the wilderness; and Israel camped there in front of the mountain.
verses.19:3: Now Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain, saying, "This is what you shall say to the house of Jacob and declare to the sons of Israel:
verses.19:4: 'You yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on wings of eagles and brought you to Myself.
verses.19:5: So now, if you will truly heed My voice and keep My covenant, then you shall be to Me a special treasure from among all the peoples, for the whole earth belongs to Me;
verses.19:6: and you yourselves shall be for Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.' These are the words that you shall speak to the sons of Israel."
verses.19:7: Then Moses came and summoned the elders of the people, and placed before them all these words that the LORD had commanded him.
verses.19:8: And all the people answered together and said, "Everything the LORD has spoken we will do." Then Moses brought back the words of the people to the LORD.
verses.19:9: The LORD said to Moses, "Look, I am coming to you in the dense cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you and may also trust in you forever." Then Moses told the words of the people to the LORD.
verses.19:10: And the LORD said to Moses, "Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their clothes,
