verses.19:11: and let them be ready for the third day, for on the third day the LORD will come down in the sight of all the people upon Mount Sinai.
verses.19:12: You shall set boundaries for the people all around, saying, 'Guard yourselves against going up on the mountain or touching its edge; anyone who touches the mountain shall certainly be put to death.
verses.19:13: No hand shall touch him; rather, he shall surely be stoned or surely be shot through. Whether beast or man, he shall not live. When the ram's horn sounds a long blast, they may go up on the mountain.'"
verses.19:14: Then Moses descended from the mountain to the people and consecrated the people, and they washed their clothes.
verses.19:15: And he said to the people, "Be ready by the third day; do not go near a woman."
verses.19:16: Now on the third day, when morning came, there were thunder and lightning, and a heavy cloud upon the mountain, and a very loud sound of a trumpet, and all the people who were in the camp trembled.
verses.19:17: Then Moses brought the people out from the camp to meet God, and they stationed themselves at the base of the mountain.
verses.19:18: Now Mount Sinai smoked completely, because the LORD had come down upon it in fire; and its smoke went up like the smoke of a furnace, and the entire mountain trembled violently.
verses.19:19: And the sound of the trumpet kept growing louder and louder; Moses would speak, and God would answer him with a voice.
verses.19:20: Then the LORD descended upon Mount Sinai, to the summit of the mountain; and the LORD summoned Moses to the summit of the mountain, and Moses went up.
verses.19:21: And the LORD said to Moses, "Go down and warn the people, or else they will break through to the LORD to look, and many of them will fall.
verses.19:22: Moreover, let the priests who draw near to the LORD consecrate themselves, or else the LORD will break out against them."
verses.19:23: Moses said to the LORD, "The people cannot go up to Mount Sinai, for You Yourself warned us, saying, 'Set boundaries around the mountain and consecrate it.'"
verses.19:24: Then the LORD said to him, "Go, descend, and then come up, you and Aaron with you; but the priests and the people must not break through to come up to the LORD, or else He will break out against them."
verses.19:25: Then Moses descended to the people and told them.
verses.20:1: Now God spoke all of these words, saying:
verses.20:2: "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves.
verses.20:3: You must not have other gods before My face.
verses.20:4: You must not make for yourself a carved image or any form of what is in the heavens above, or what is on the earth beneath, or what is in the waters below the earth.
verses.20:5: You must not bow down to them nor serve them, for I am the LORD your God, a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of fathers upon children, to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me,
verses.20:6: yet showing loyal love to thousands, to those who love Me and to those who keep My commands.
verses.20:7: You must not take up the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not acquit the one who takes up His name in vain.
verses.20:8: Remember the Sabbath day, to set it apart as holy.
verses.20:9: For six days you are to labor and do all your work,
verses.20:10: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. You must not do any work, neither you, nor your son or your daughter, your male slave or your female slave, your livestock, nor your resident foreigner who is within your gates.
verses.20:11: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea and everything that is in them, and He rested on the seventh day. For this reason, the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy.
verses.20:12: Honor your father and your mother, so that your days may lengthen upon the land that the LORD your God is giving to you.
verses.20:16: You must not testify as a false witness against your neighbor.
verses.20:17: You must not covet your neighbor's house; you must not covet your neighbor's wife, nor his male slave or his female slave, nor his ox or his donkey, nor anything belonging to your neighbor."
verses.20:18: Now all the people were seeing the thunder, the lightning flashes, the sound of the ram's horn, and the mountain smoking. When the people saw it, they shook and stood far off.
verses.20:19: And they said to Moses, "You speak with us, and we will listen; but do not let God speak with us, or else we will die."
verses.20:20: Then Moses said to the people, "Do not be afraid, for God has come to test you, and so that the fear of Him will be before your faces, in order that you do not sin."
verses.20:21: So the people stood far off, and Moses approached the thick darkness where God was.
verses.20:22: Then the LORD said to Moses, "This is what you are to say to the sons of Israel: 'You yourselves have seen that I have spoken with you from the heavens.
verses.20:23: You must not make gods alongside Me; gods of silver or gods of gold you must not make for yourselves.
verses.20:24: You are to make for Me an altar of earth and sacrifice upon it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your flock and your herd. At every place where I make My name remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
verses.20:25: And if you make an altar of stones for Me, you must not build it out of cut stones, for if you swing your chisel against it, you will profane it.
verses.20:26: And you must not climb up by steps onto My altar, so that your nakedness will not be uncovered upon it.'"
verses.21:1: "Now these are the legal rulings that you are to place before them.
verses.21:2: When you buy a Hebrew slave, for six years he is to serve, and in the seventh he is to go out free, at no cost.
verses.21:3: If he comes in by himself, he is to go out by himself; if he has a wife, then his wife is to go out with him.
verses.21:4: If his master gives a wife to him, and she bears sons or daughters for him, the woman and her children are to belong to her master, while he is to go out by himself.
verses.21:5: Yet if the slave firmly says, 'I love my master, my wife, and my children; I am not going out free,'
verses.21:6: then his master must bring him near to God, and bring him near to the door or to the doorpost; and his master must pierce his ear with an awl, and he will serve him forever.
verses.21:7: Now when a man sells his daughter as a female slave, she must not go out in the manner that the male slaves go out.
verses.21:8: If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master, who designated her for himself, then he must allow her to be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to a foreign people, because he has dealt treacherously with her.
verses.21:9: And if he designates her for his son, he must act toward her according to the legal right of daughters.
verses.21:10: If he takes another woman for himself, he must not diminish her food, her clothing, or her marital rights.
verses.21:11: And if he does not do these three things for her, then she is to go out at no cost, without money.
verses.21:12: One who strikes a man so that he dies must certainly be put to death.
verses.21:13: Yet if he did not lie in wait, and God caused it to come into his hand, then I will appoint a place for you where he can flee.
verses.21:14: But if a man acts presumptuously against his neighbor to kill him with cunning, you must take him from beside My altar to die.
verses.21:15: And one who strikes his father or his mother must certainly be put to death.
verses.21:16: And one who curses his father or his mother must certainly be put to death.
verses.21:17: And one who steals a person, whether he has sold him or he is found in his hand, must certainly be put to death.
verses.21:18: And when men quarrel, and one strikes his neighbor with a stone or with a fist, and he does not die but falls bedridden,
verses.21:19: if he rises and walks about outside on his staff, then the one who struck him is to be acquitted; only he must pay for his lost time and see that he is completely healed.
verses.21:20: And when a man strikes his male slave or his female slave with a rod, and the slave dies under his hand, the slave must certainly be avenged.
verses.21:21: However, if the slave survives a day or two, he is not to be avenged, for the slave is his money.
verses.21:22: And when men fight each other and strike a pregnant woman so that her children come out, yet no harm occurs, he must certainly be fined according to what the woman's husband imposes upon him, and he must pay as assessed by the judges.
verses.21:23: But if harm occurs, then you must give a life for a life,
verses.21:24: an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot,
verses.21:25: a burn for a burn, a wound for a wound, a welt for a welt.
verses.21:26: And when a man strikes the eye of his male slave or the eye of his female slave and destroys it, he must release him into freedom in place of his eye.
verses.21:27: And if he knocks out a tooth of his male slave or a tooth of his female slave, he must release him into freedom in place of his tooth.
verses.21:28: And when an ox gores a man or a woman so that he or she dies, the ox must certainly be stoned and its flesh must not be eaten, while the owner of the ox is guiltless.
verses.21:29: However, if it was an ox given to goring in the past, and its owner had been warned yet did not keep it under guard, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox must be stoned, and its owner as well must be put to death.
verses.21:30: If a ransom is imposed upon him, then he must pay as the redemption price for his life all that is imposed upon him.
verses.21:31: Whether it gores a son or gores a daughter, according to this ruling it must be done to him.
verses.21:32: If the ox gores a male slave or a female slave, the owner must pay thirty shekels of silver to the slave's master, and the ox must be stoned.
verses.21:33: And when a man uncovers a pit, or when a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
verses.21:34: the owner of the pit must make restitution; he must pay back money to its owner, and the dead animal will belong to him.
verses.21:35: And when a man's ox strikes his neighbor's ox so that it dies, then they must sell the live ox and divide its money in half, and the dead animal as well they must divide in half.
verses.21:36: Or if it was known that it was an ox given to goring in the past, yet its owner did not keep it under guard, he must certainly make restitution of an ox in place of the ox, and the dead animal will belong to him.
verses.21:37: When a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, he must make restitution of five from the herd in place of the ox and four from the flock in place of the sheep."
verses.22:1: If the thief is found in the act of breaking in, and he is struck and dies, there is no bloodguilt for him.
verses.22:2: If the sun has risen upon him, there is bloodguilt for him. He must certainly pay restitution; if he possesses nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
verses.22:3: If what was stolen is actually found alive in his hand, whether ox, donkey, or sheep, he shall pay double.
verses.22:4: When a man causes a field or a vineyard to be grazed, and releases his livestock so that it grazes in another's field, he shall pay restitution from the best of his field and the best of his vineyard.
verses.22:5: When fire breaks out and catches thorns, so that stacked grain or the standing grain or the field is consumed, the one who kindled the blaze must certainly pay restitution.
verses.22:6: When a man gives money or articles to his neighbor to keep, and it is stolen from the man's house, if the thief is found, he shall pay double.
verses.22:7: If the thief is not found, then the owner of the house shall draw near to God to establish whether he has stretched out his hand to his neighbor's goods.
verses.22:8: In every case of transgression, whether for an ox, for a donkey, for a sheep, for a garment, or for any lost item of which someone says, "This is it," the case of the two of them shall come to God; the one whom God declares guilty shall pay double to his neighbor.
verses.22:9: When a man gives a donkey, or an ox, or a sheep, or any animal to his neighbor to keep, and it dies or is injured or is carried off with no one seeing,
verses.22:10: an oath by the LORD shall be between the two of them that he has not stretched out his hand to his neighbor's goods. Its owner shall accept it, and he shall not pay restitution.
verses.22:11: But if it is indeed stolen from him, he shall pay restitution to its owner.
verses.22:12: If it is indeed torn to pieces, he shall bring it as evidence; for what was torn he shall not pay restitution.
verses.22:13: And when a man borrows something from his neighbor, and it is injured or dies without its owner being with it, he must certainly pay restitution.
verses.22:14: If its owner is with it, he shall not pay restitution; if it was hired, it came for its rental fee.
verses.22:15: And if a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed and lies with her, he must certainly pay the bride-price for her to be his wife.
verses.22:16: If her father firmly refuses to give her to him, he shall weigh out silver according to the bride-price for virgins.
verses.22:17: You shall not let a sorceress live.
verses.22:18: Anyone who lies with an animal must certainly be put to death.
verses.22:19: Anyone who sacrifices to any god, except to the LORD alone, shall be devoted to destruction.
verses.22:20: You shall not mistreat a sojourner, nor shall you oppress him, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
verses.22:21: You shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child.
verses.22:22: If you afflict him in any way, and he indeed cries out to Me, I will certainly hear his cry.
verses.22:23: And My anger will burn, and I will kill you by the sword; your wives will become widows, and your children will be fatherless.
verses.22:24: If you lend money to My people, to the poor person with you, you shall not be like a creditor to him; you shall not impose interest upon him.
verses.22:25: If you indeed take your neighbor's garment as a pledge, you shall return it to him by sunset.
verses.22:26: For that is his only covering; it is his garment for his skin. In what will he sleep? And when he cries out to Me, I will hear, for I am gracious.
verses.22:27: You shall not revile God, nor shall you curse a leader among your people.
verses.22:28: You shall not delay your full yield or your flowing juice; you shall give the firstborn of your sons to Me.
verses.22:29: You shall do likewise with your ox and your flock: for seven days it shall be with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.
verses.22:30: And you shall be holy people to Me, and you shall not eat meat torn in the field; you shall throw it to the dogs.
verses.23:1: You shall not carry a false report; do not put your hand with a wicked person to be a malicious witness.
verses.23:2: You shall not follow after the many for evil, nor shall you testify in a dispute by turning aside after the many to pervert justice.
verses.23:3: And you shall not favor a poor person in his dispute.
verses.23:4: If you come upon your enemy's ox or his donkey straying, you must certainly bring it back to him.
verses.23:5: If you see the donkey of someone who hates you lying under its burden, you must hold back from abandoning it to him; you must certainly free it with him.
verses.23:6: You shall not pervert the justice of your needy one in his dispute.
verses.23:7: Stay far from a false matter, and do not kill an innocent and righteous person, for I will not declare a wicked person righteous.
verses.23:8: And you shall not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the open-eyed and twists the words of the righteous.
verses.23:9: And you shall not oppress a sojourner; you yourselves know the soul of a sojourner, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
verses.23:10: And for six years you shall sow your land and gather its produce,
verses.23:11: but in the seventh year you shall release it and leave it fallow, so that the needy of your people may eat, and what they leave the wild animals of the field may eat. Likewise you shall do with your vineyard and your olive grove.
verses.23:12: For six days you shall do your work, and on the seventh day you shall stop working, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your female servant and the sojourner may be refreshed.
verses.23:13: And be careful regarding everything that I have said to you; you shall not mention the name of other gods; it shall not be heard from your mouth.
verses.23:14: Three times in the year you shall celebrate a festival to Me.
verses.23:15: You shall keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread: for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, just as I commanded you, at the appointed time of the month of Abib, for in it you went out from Egypt; and no one shall appear before Me empty-handed.
verses.23:16: And you shall keep the Festival of Harvest, of the firstfruits of your labors that you sow in the field, and the Festival of Ingathering at the close of the year, when you gather in your labors from the field.
verses.23:17: Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Sovereign, the LORD.
verses.23:18: You shall not offer the blood of My sacrifice together with what is leavened, nor shall the fat of My festival remain overnight until morning.
verses.23:19: You shall bring the choicest of the firstfruits of your ground to the house of the LORD your God. You shall not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
verses.23:20: Look, I am sending an angel ahead of you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.
verses.23:21: Watch yourself in his presence and listen to his voice; do not defy him, for he will not forgive your transgression, because My name is within him.
verses.23:22: But if you indeed listen to his voice and do everything that I speak, then I will be an enemy to your enemies, and I will oppose those who oppose you.
verses.23:23: For My angel will go ahead of you and bring you to the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
verses.23:24: You shall not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor act according to their deeds; rather, you must completely tear them down and thoroughly smash their sacred pillars.
verses.23:25: You shall serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water, and I will remove illness from your midst.
verses.23:26: There shall not be one who miscarries or is barren in your land; the number of your days I will fulfill.
verses.23:27: I will send My dread ahead of you, and I will throw into panic all the people among whom you come, and I will cause all your enemies to turn their backs to you.
verses.23:28: And I will send the hornets ahead of you, and they will drive out the Hivites, the Canaanites, and the Hittites from before you.
verses.23:29: I will not drive them out from before you in one year, or else the land will become desolate and the wild animals of the field will multiply against you.
verses.23:30: Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you become fruitful and inherit the land.
verses.23:31: And I will fix your border from the Red Sea to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River, for I will give into your hand the inhabitants of the land, and you shall drive them out from before you.
verses.23:32: You shall not make a covenant with them or with their gods.
verses.23:33: They shall not dwell in your land, or else they will cause you to sin against Me; for if you serve their gods, it will certainly become a snare to you.
verses.24:1: Now to Moses He said, "Come up to the LORD, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy from the elders of Israel, and bow down from a distance.
verses.24:2: Moses alone shall approach the LORD, while they shall not approach, and the people shall not go up with him."
verses.24:3: Then Moses came and recounted to the people all the words of the LORD and all the rulings. And all the people responded with one voice and said, "We will do all the words that the LORD has spoken."
verses.24:4: So Moses wrote all the words of the LORD. Then he rose early in the morning and built an altar at the base of the mountain, with twelve standing stones for the twelve tribes of Israel.
verses.24:5: Then he sent young men of the sons of Israel, and they offered up burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings of bulls to the LORD.
verses.24:6: Moses took half of the blood and placed it in the basins, and half of the blood he splashed on the altar.
verses.24:7: Then he took the scroll of the covenant and read it in the ears of the people. And they said, "Everything that the LORD has spoken we will do and we will obey."
verses.24:8: So Moses took the blood and splashed it on the people, and he said, "Here is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you on the basis of all these words."
verses.24:9: Then Moses went up, along with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy from the elders of Israel.
verses.24:10: And they saw the God of Israel, and beneath His feet was something like a work of lapis lazuli pavement, and like the very heavens in purity.
verses.24:11: Yet against the nobles of the sons of Israel He did not extend His hand; and they gazed on God, and they ate and drank.
verses.24:12: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Come up to Me onto the mountain and stay there, and I will give you the tablets of stone, and the law and the commandment that I have written to instruct them."
verses.24:13: Then Moses rose, together with Joshua his attendant, and Moses went up to the mountain of God.
verses.24:14: Now to the elders he said, "Stay here for us until we return to you. Look, Aaron and Hur are with you; whoever has a dispute, let him approach them."
verses.24:15: So Moses went up onto the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
verses.24:16: And the glory of the LORD dwelt on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. Then He called to Moses on the seventh day from within the cloud.
verses.24:17: And the appearance of the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire on the summit of the mountain, before the eyes of the sons of Israel.
verses.24:18: Then Moses went into the midst of the cloud and went up onto the mountain, and Moses remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
verses.25:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.25:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel so that they take up a contribution for Me; from every man whose heart prompts him, you shall take My contribution.
verses.25:3: And this is the contribution that you shall take from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
verses.25:4: blue, purple, and crimson yarn, fine linen, and goat hair;
verses.25:5: ram skins dyed red, dugong skins, and acacia wood;
verses.25:7: onyx stones and stones for mounting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece.
verses.25:8: And they shall make a sanctuary for Me, and I will dwell in their midst.
verses.25:9: According to everything that I am showing you, the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its furnishings, so you shall make it.
verses.25:10: And they shall make an ark of acacia wood; its length shall be two and a half cubits, its width one and a half cubits, and its height one and a half cubits.
verses.25:11: And you shall overlay it with pure gold; inside and outside you shall overlay it, and you shall make a gold molding on it all around.
verses.25:12: And you shall cast four gold rings for it and place them on its four feet, two rings on its one side and two rings on its other side.
verses.25:13: And you shall make poles of acacia wood, and you shall overlay them with gold.
verses.25:14: And you shall insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, so as to carry the ark with them.
verses.25:15: In the rings of the ark the poles shall remain; they shall not come out from it.
verses.25:16: And you shall place into the ark the testimony that I will give to you.
verses.25:17: And you shall make an atonement cover of pure gold; its length shall be two and a half cubits, and its width one and a half cubits.
verses.25:18: You shall also make two cherubim of gold; you shall make them of hammered work at the two ends of the atonement cover.
verses.25:19: Make one cherub at this end and one cherub at the other end; out of the atonement cover itself you shall make the cherubim on its two ends.
verses.25:20: The cherubim shall spread their wings upward, sheltering the atonement cover with their wings, with their faces toward one another; the faces of the cherubim shall be toward the atonement cover.
verses.25:21: And you shall set the atonement cover on top of the ark, and into the ark you shall place the testimony that I will give to you.
verses.25:22: And I will meet with you there, and I will speak with you from above the atonement cover, from between the two cherubim which are on the ark of the testimony, concerning everything that I will command you for the sons of Israel.
verses.25:23: And you shall make a table of acacia wood; its length shall be two cubits, its width one cubit, and its height one and a half cubits.
verses.25:24: And you shall overlay it with pure gold, and you shall make a gold molding for it all around.
verses.25:25: And you shall make a handbreadth frame for it all around, and you shall make a gold molding for its frame all around.
verses.25:26: And you shall make four gold rings for it, and place the rings on the four corners that belong to its four legs.
verses.25:27: Right beside the frame the rings shall be, as housings for poles to carry the table.
verses.25:28: And you shall make the poles of acacia wood, and you shall overlay them with gold, and the table shall be carried by them.
verses.25:29: And you shall make its platters, its ladles, its pitchers, and its bowls with which drink offerings are poured; of pure gold you shall make them.
verses.25:30: And you shall place bread of the Presence on the table before Me continually.
verses.25:31: And you shall make a lampstand of pure gold. Of hammered work the lampstand shall be made; its base and its shaft, its cups, its knobs, and its blossoms shall be of one piece with it.
verses.25:32: And six branches shall extend from its sides: three lampstand branches from one side of it, and three lampstand branches from its other side.
verses.25:33: Three almond-shaped cups shall be on one branch, a knob and a blossom, and three almond-shaped cups on the next branch, a knob and a blossom; so for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
verses.25:34: And on the lampstand there shall be four almond-shaped cups, with its knobs and its blossoms.
verses.25:35: And a knob shall be beneath two branches, of one piece with it, and a knob beneath two branches, of one piece with it, and a knob beneath two branches, of one piece with it, for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
verses.25:36: Their knobs and their branches shall be of one piece with it; all of it shall be a single hammered work of pure gold.
verses.25:37: And you shall make its lamps, seven of them, and its lamps shall be mounted so that they cast light over the area in front of it.
verses.25:38: And its tongs and its firepans shall be of pure gold.
verses.25:39: Out of a talent of pure gold it shall be made, along with all these utensils.
verses.25:40: And see to it that you make them according to their pattern, which you are being shown on the mountain."
verses.26:1: Now you shall make the tabernacle out of ten curtains of twisted fine linen, and blue, purple, and crimson; you shall make them with cherubim, the work of a skilled designer.
verses.26:2: The length of each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits; there shall be one measurement for all the curtains.
verses.26:3: Five of the curtains shall be joined one to another, and five curtains shall be joined one to another.
verses.26:4: And you shall make loops of blue on the edge of the one curtain at the end of the joined set, and you shall do likewise on the edge of the outermost curtain in the second joined set.
verses.26:5: You shall make fifty loops on the one curtain, and you shall make fifty loops at the end of the curtain that is in the second joined set; the loops shall correspond one to another.
verses.26:6: And you shall make fifty clasps of gold, and join the curtains one to another with the clasps, so that the tabernacle shall be one.
verses.26:7: And you shall make curtains of goat hair for a tent over the tabernacle; you shall make them as eleven curtains.
verses.26:8: The length of each curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits; there shall be one measurement for the eleven curtains.
verses.26:9: And you shall join five of the curtains by themselves and six of the curtains by themselves, and you shall double over the sixth curtain at the front of the tent.
verses.26:10: And you shall make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain that is outermost in the joined set, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain of the second joined set.
verses.26:11: And you shall make fifty clasps of bronze, and put the clasps into the loops and join the tent together, so that it shall be one.
verses.26:12: And as for the overhanging excess of the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that remains over shall hang down over the back of the tabernacle.
verses.26:13: And the cubit on this side and the cubit on that side of what remains over in the length of the curtains of the tent shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle, on this side and on that side, to cover it.
verses.26:14: And you shall make a covering for the tent of ram skins dyed red, and a covering of dugong skins on top.
verses.26:15: And you shall make the planks for the tabernacle of acacia wood, standing upright.
verses.26:16: Ten cubits shall be the length of a plank, and a cubit and a half the width of each plank.
verses.26:17: Each plank shall have two tenons, set parallel one to another; so you shall do for all the planks of the tabernacle.
verses.26:18: And you shall make the planks for the tabernacle: twenty planks for the south side, southward.
verses.26:19: And you shall make forty bases of silver under the twenty planks: two bases under one plank for its two tenons, and two bases under the next plank for its two tenons.
verses.26:20: And for the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, there shall be twenty planks,
verses.26:21: and their forty bases of silver: two bases under one plank, and two bases under the next plank.
verses.26:22: And for the rear of the tabernacle, westward, you shall make six planks.
verses.26:23: And you shall make two planks for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.
verses.26:24: And they shall be doubled at the bottom, and together they shall be complete at the top, at the single ring; so it shall be for both of them; they shall be for the two corners.
verses.26:25: So there shall be eight planks with their bases of silver, sixteen bases: two bases under one plank, and two bases under the next plank.
verses.26:26: And you shall make crossbars of acacia wood: five for the planks of the one side of the tabernacle,
verses.26:27: and five crossbars for the planks of the second side of the tabernacle, and five crossbars for the planks of the side of the tabernacle at the rear, westward.
verses.26:28: And the middle crossbar, in the center of the planks, shall run through from end to end.
verses.26:29: And you shall overlay the planks with gold, and make their rings of gold as housings for the crossbars; and you shall overlay the crossbars with gold.
verses.26:30: And you shall set up the tabernacle according to its specification that you were shown on the mountain.
verses.26:31: And you shall make a veil of blue, purple, crimson, and twisted fine linen; it shall be made with cherubim, the work of a skilled designer.
verses.26:32: And you shall hang it on four pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold, their hooks of gold, on four bases of silver.
verses.26:33: And you shall hang the veil beneath the clasps, and bring the ark of the testimony in there, inside the veil; and the veil shall separate the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies for you.
verses.26:34: And you shall put the atonement cover on the ark of the testimony in the Holy of Holies.
verses.26:35: And you shall place the table outside the veil, with the lampstand across from the table on the south side of the tabernacle, while the table you shall put on the north side.
verses.26:36: And you shall make a screen for the entrance of the tent of blue, purple, crimson, and twisted fine linen, the work of an embroiderer.
verses.26:37: And you shall make five pillars of acacia wood for the screen and overlay them with gold, their hooks of gold; and you shall cast five bases of bronze for them.
verses.27:1: And you shall make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide; the altar shall be square, and its height shall be three cubits.
verses.27:2: And you shall make its horns on its four corners; its horns shall be integral with it, and you shall overlay it with bronze.
verses.27:3: And you shall make its pots to clear away its ashes, along with its shovels, its basins, its forks, and its firepans; you shall make all its utensils of bronze.
verses.27:4: And you shall make for it a grating, a meshwork of bronze, and on the mesh you shall make four rings of bronze at its four corners.
verses.27:5: And you shall place it under the ledge of the altar from below, so that the mesh extends to half the height of the altar.
verses.27:6: You shall also make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and you shall overlay them with bronze.
verses.27:7: And its poles shall be inserted into the rings, so that the poles are on the two sides of the altar when carrying it.
verses.27:8: You shall make it hollow, of boards; just as was shown to you on the mountain, so they shall make it.
verses.27:9: And you shall make the courtyard of the tabernacle. On the south side, southward, there shall be hangings for the courtyard of twisted fine linen, one hundred cubits in length for the one side,
verses.27:10: and its pillars shall be twenty, and their twenty bases of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands shall be of silver.
verses.27:11: And likewise for the north side along the length, there shall be hangings one hundred cubits in length, and its pillars shall be twenty, and their twenty bases of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands shall be of silver.
verses.27:12: And for the width of the courtyard on the west side, there shall be hangings of fifty cubits; their pillars shall be ten, and their bases ten.
verses.27:13: And the width of the courtyard on the east side, toward the sunrise, shall be fifty cubits.
verses.27:14: There shall be fifteen cubits of hangings for the one flank; their pillars shall be three, and their bases three.
verses.27:15: And for the second flank, fifteen cubits of hangings; their pillars shall be three, and their bases three.
verses.27:16: And for the gate of the courtyard there shall be a screen of twenty cubits, of blue, purple, crimson, and twisted fine linen, the work of an embroiderer; its pillars shall be four, and its bases four.
verses.27:17: All the pillars of the courtyard all around shall be banded with silver; their hooks shall be of silver, and their bases of bronze.
verses.27:18: The length of the courtyard shall be one hundred cubits, and the width fifty cubits at each end, and the height five cubits, of twisted fine linen, with their bases of bronze.
verses.27:19: All the utensils of the tabernacle in all its service, and all its pegs, and all the pegs of the courtyard, shall be of bronze.
verses.27:20: Now you shall command the sons of Israel so that they bring to you pure, pounded olive oil for the lighting, to cause a lamp to burn continually.
verses.27:21: In the tent of meeting, outside the veil that is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall set it in order from evening until morning before the LORD; it is an everlasting statute for their generations from the sons of Israel.
verses.28:1: Now you, bring near to yourself Aaron your brother, and his sons with him, from the midst of the sons of Israel, so that he may serve as priest to Me—Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron.
verses.28:2: And you shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother, for glory and for splendor.
verses.28:3: And you shall speak to all who are wise of heart, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, and they shall make the garments of Aaron to consecrate him, so that he may serve as priest to Me.
verses.28:4: And these are the garments that they shall make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a tunic of checkered weave, a turban, and a sash. They shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother and for his sons, so that he may serve as priest to Me.
verses.28:5: And they shall take the gold, the blue, the purple, the crimson, and the fine linen.
verses.28:6: And they shall make the ephod of gold, blue, purple, crimson, and twisted fine linen, the work of a skilled designer.
verses.28:7: It shall have two joining shoulder pieces at its two edges, and it shall be joined together.
verses.28:8: And the woven band for fastening it, which is on it, shall be like its workmanship, of one piece with it: of gold, blue, purple, crimson, and twisted fine linen.
verses.28:9: And you shall take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel:
verses.28:10: six of their names on the one stone, and the names of the remaining six on the second stone, according to their births.
verses.28:11: Like the work of a stone craftsman, as the engravings of a signet, you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel; you shall make them enclosed in gold filigree settings.
verses.28:12: And you shall place the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of reminder for the sons of Israel; and Aaron shall bear their names before the LORD on his two shoulders as a reminder.
verses.28:13: And you shall make gold filigree settings.
verses.28:14: And two chains of pure gold you shall make twisted, of braided work; and you shall attach the braided chains onto the filigree settings.
verses.28:15: And you shall make a breastpiece of judgment, the work of a skilled designer; like the work of the ephod you shall make it: of gold, blue, purple, crimson, and twisted fine linen you shall make it.
verses.28:16: It shall be square, folded double: a span its length and a span its width.
verses.28:17: And you shall fill it with a mounting of stones, four rows of stones: a row of carnelian, topaz, and emerald shall be the first row.
verses.28:18: And the second row shall be turquoise, lapis lazuli, and chalcedony.
verses.28:19: And the third row shall be jacinth, agate, and amethyst.
verses.28:20: And the fourth row shall be beryl, onyx, and jasper; they shall be framed in gold filigree in their mountings.
verses.28:21: And the stones shall be according to the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names; like the engravings of a signet, each according to his name, they shall be for the twelve tribes.
verses.28:22: And you shall make on the breastpiece twisted chains of braided work, of pure gold.
verses.28:29: And you shall attach the two braided cords of gold to the two rings at the edges of the breastpiece. And the two ends of the two braided cords you shall attach to the two filigree settings, and place them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod at its front. And Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel in the breastpiece of judgment on his heart when he enters the holy place, as a reminder before the LORD continually.
verses.28:30: And you shall place into the breastpiece of judgment the Urim and the Thummim, and they shall be on the heart of Aaron when he comes before the LORD; thus Aaron shall bear the judgment of the sons of Israel on his heart before the LORD continually.
verses.28:31: And you shall make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue.
verses.28:32: And its head opening shall be in its center; it shall have a border all around its opening, the work of a weaver; it shall be like the opening of a coat of mail, so that it will not be torn.
verses.28:33: And you shall make on its hem pomegranates of blue, purple, and crimson, on its hem all around, and bells of gold between them all around:
verses.28:34: a bell of gold and a pomegranate, a bell of gold and a pomegranate, on the hem of the robe all around.
verses.28:35: And it shall be on Aaron for ministering, and its sound shall be heard when he enters the holy place before the LORD and when he goes out, so that he will not die.
verses.28:36: And you shall make a plate of pure gold, and you shall engrave on it, as the engravings of a signet, "Holiness to the LORD."
verses.28:37: And you shall place it on a blue cord, and it shall be on the turban; it shall be at the front of the turban.
verses.28:38: And it shall be on Aaron's forehead, and Aaron shall bear the guilt of the holy things that the sons of Israel consecrate, regarding all their holy gifts; and it shall be on his forehead continually, for their acceptance before the LORD.
verses.28:39: And you shall weave the tunic of fine linen in a checkered pattern, and you shall make a turban of fine linen, and you shall make a sash, the work of an embroiderer.
verses.28:40: And for the sons of Aaron you shall make tunics, and you shall make sashes for them, and you shall make caps for them, for glory and for splendor.
verses.28:41: And you shall clothe Aaron your brother and his sons with him in them, and you shall anoint them, ordain them, and consecrate them, so that they may serve as priests to Me.
verses.28:42: And make for them linen undergarments to cover naked flesh; they shall reach from the waist to the thighs.
verses.28:43: And they shall be on Aaron and on his sons when they enter the tent of meeting, or when they approach the altar to minister in the holy place, so that they will not bear guilt and die. It shall be a perpetual statute for him and for his descendants after him.
verses.29:1: Now this is the thing that you shall do for them to consecrate them to serve as priests to Me: take one bull from the herd and two rams without blemish,
verses.29:2: and unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil. You shall make them of fine wheat flour.
verses.29:3: You shall place them in one basket and present them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
verses.29:4: Then you shall bring Aaron and his sons near to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
verses.29:5: You shall take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastpiece, and fasten it on him with the woven band of the ephod.
verses.29:6: You shall set the turban on his head and place the holy crown on the turban.
verses.29:7: And you shall take the anointing oil, pour it onto his head, and anoint him.
verses.29:8: You shall bring his sons near and clothe them with tunics.
verses.29:9: You shall tie sashes around them, Aaron and his sons, and bind caps on them; and the priesthood shall be theirs by a perpetual statute. So you shall ordain Aaron and his sons.
verses.29:10: Then you shall bring the bull near in front of the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the bull's head.
verses.29:11: You shall slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.29:12: You shall take some of the bull's blood and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, and all the blood you shall pour out at the base of the altar.
verses.29:13: You shall take all the fat that covers the entrails, the lobe on the liver, and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, and offer them in smoke on the altar.
verses.29:14: But the flesh of the bull, its hide, and its dung you shall burn with fire outside the camp; it is a sin offering.
verses.29:15: You shall then take the one ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the ram's head.
verses.29:16: You shall slaughter the ram, take its blood, and dash it against the altar all around.
verses.29:17: Then you shall cut the ram into its pieces, wash its entrails and its legs, and place them with its pieces and with its head.
verses.29:18: You shall offer the entire ram in smoke on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing fragrance; it is a fire offering to the LORD.
verses.29:19: Then you shall take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the ram's head.
verses.29:20: You shall slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear and on the lobes of his sons' right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet, and dash the blood against the altar all around.
verses.29:21: Then you shall take some of the blood that is on the altar and some of the anointing oil, and sprinkle them on Aaron and on his garments, and on his sons and on his sons' garments with him. And he shall become holy, along with his garments, his sons, and his sons' garments with him.
verses.29:22: You shall also take from the ram the fat and the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, and the right thigh, for it is a ram of ordination;
verses.29:23: and one round loaf of bread, one cake of oiled bread, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
verses.29:24: You shall place all of them on the palms of Aaron and on the palms of his sons, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
verses.29:25: Then you shall take them from their hands and offer them in smoke on the altar on top of the burnt offering, for a pleasing fragrance before the LORD; it is a fire offering to the LORD.
verses.29:26: You shall take the breast from the ram of ordination that is for Aaron and wave it as a wave offering before the LORD, and it shall be your portion.
verses.29:27: You shall consecrate the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution, which was waved and which was lifted up from the ram of ordination, from what is for Aaron and from what is for his sons.
verses.29:28: It shall belong to Aaron and to his sons as a perpetual due from the sons of Israel, for it is a contribution; and it shall be a contribution from the sons of Israel from the sacrifices of their peace offerings, their contribution to the LORD.
verses.29:29: The holy garments of Aaron shall belong to his sons after him, for them to be anointed in them and to be ordained in them.
verses.29:30: For seven days the priest in his place from among his sons, who enters the tent of meeting to minister in the holy place, shall wear them.
verses.29:31: And the ram of ordination you shall take, and you shall boil its flesh in a holy place.
verses.29:32: Aaron and his sons shall eat the ram's flesh and the bread that is in the basket at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.29:33: They shall eat those things by which atonement was made, to ordain them, to consecrate them; but an outsider shall not eat of them, for they are holy.
verses.29:34: And if any of the flesh of ordination or of the bread remains until the morning, then you shall burn what remains with fire; it shall not be eaten, for it is holy.
verses.29:35: So you shall do for Aaron and for his sons, in accordance with all that I have commanded you; for seven days you shall ordain them.
verses.29:36: You shall offer a bull as a sin offering each day for atonement, and you shall purify the altar when you make atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
verses.29:37: For seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and consecrate it; and the altar shall be most holy, and anything that touches the altar shall become holy.
verses.29:38: And this is what you shall offer upon the altar: two year-old lambs each day, continually.
verses.29:39: The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the second lamb you shall offer at twilight.
verses.29:40: With the one lamb there shall be a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a fourth of a hin of beaten oil, and a drink offering of a fourth of a hin of wine.
verses.29:41: And the second lamb you shall offer at twilight; you shall do with it as with the morning grain offering and its drink offering, for a pleasing fragrance, a fire offering to the LORD.
verses.29:42: It is a continual burnt offering for your generations at the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD, where I will meet with you to speak to you there.
verses.29:43: And there I will meet with the sons of Israel, and it will be consecrated by My glory.
verses.29:44: I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar, and Aaron and his sons I will consecrate to serve as priests to Me.
verses.29:45: And I will dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel, and I will be God to them.
verses.29:46: And they will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out from the land of Egypt so that I might dwell in their midst; I am the LORD their God.
verses.30:1: "And you shall make an altar for burning incense; out of acacia wood you shall make it.
verses.30:2: One cubit shall be its length and one cubit its width; it shall be square, and its height shall be two cubits; its horns shall be part of it.
verses.30:3: And you shall overlay it with pure gold—its top, its walls all around, and its horns—and you shall make a gold molding for it all around.
verses.30:4: And you shall make two gold rings for it beneath its molding; you shall make them on two of its sides, on its two opposite sides, and they shall serve as holders for poles to carry it by them.
verses.30:5: And you shall make the poles out of acacia wood, and you shall overlay them with gold.
verses.30:6: And you shall set it in front of the veil that is by the ark of the testimony, in front of the atonement cover that is over the testimony, where I will meet with you.
verses.30:7: And Aaron shall burn incense of aromatic spices on it; morning by morning, when he tends the lamps, he shall burn it.
verses.30:8: And when Aaron lights the lamps at twilight, he shall burn it, a continual incense before the LORD throughout your generations.
verses.30:9: You shall not offer up unauthorized incense on it, nor a burnt offering, nor a grain offering; and you shall not pour out a drink offering on it.
verses.30:10: And Aaron shall make atonement on its horns once a year; with some of the blood of the sin offering of atonement he shall make atonement on it once a year throughout your generations. It is most holy to the LORD."
verses.30:11: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.30:12: "When you take a census of the sons of Israel for their numbering, each man shall give a ransom for his life to the LORD when they are numbered, so that there will not be a plague among them when they are numbered.
verses.30:13: This is what everyone who passes over to those who are numbered shall give: half a shekel by the sanctuary shekel—the shekel is twenty gerahs—half a shekel as a contribution to the LORD.
verses.30:14: Everyone who passes over to those who are numbered, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the LORD's contribution.
verses.30:15: The rich shall not exceed and the poor shall not fall short of the half shekel in giving the LORD's contribution to make atonement for your lives.
verses.30:16: And you shall take the atonement silver from the sons of Israel and assign it for the service of the tent of meeting, and it shall serve for the sons of Israel as a memorial before the LORD to make atonement for your lives."
verses.30:17: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.30:18: "You shall also make a bronze basin, and its stand of bronze, for washing; and you shall place it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water into it.
verses.30:19: And from it Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet.
verses.30:20: When they go into the tent of meeting, they shall wash with water so that they will not die; or when they approach the altar to minister, to burn an offering by fire to the LORD,
verses.30:21: they shall wash their hands and their feet so that they will not die; and it shall be an everlasting statute for them, for him and for his offspring throughout their generations."
verses.30:22: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.30:23: "And you, take for yourself the finest spices: five hundred shekels of flowing myrrh, half as much of fragrant cinnamon—two hundred and fifty—and two hundred and fifty of fragrant cane,
verses.30:24: and five hundred of cassia by the sanctuary shekel, and a hin of olive oil.
verses.30:25: And you shall make it into a holy anointing oil, a compounded perfume, the work of a perfumer; it shall be a holy anointing oil.
verses.30:26: And you shall anoint with it the tent of meeting, the ark of the testimony,
verses.30:27: the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, the incense altar,
verses.30:28: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin and its stand.
verses.30:29: And you shall consecrate them, and they shall be most holy; anything that touches them shall become holy.
verses.30:30: You shall also anoint Aaron and his sons, and consecrate them to serve as priests to Me.
verses.30:31: And you shall speak to the sons of Israel, saying, 'This shall be to Me a holy anointing oil throughout your generations.
verses.30:32: It shall not be poured on human flesh, and according to its composition you shall not make any like it; it is holy, and holy it shall be to you.
verses.30:33: Anyone who compounds any like it, or who puts some of it on an unauthorized person, shall be cut off from his people.'"
verses.30:34: And the LORD said to Moses, "Take for yourself aromatic spices—stacte, onycha, and galbanum—aromatic spices with pure frankincense; there shall be an equal portion of each.
verses.30:35: And you shall make it into incense, a perfume, the work of a perfumer, seasoned with salt, pure and holy.
verses.30:36: And you shall grind some of it very fine and place some of it in front of the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you; it shall be most holy to you.
verses.30:37: And as for the incense that you shall make, according to its composition you shall not make any for yourselves; to you it shall be holy to the LORD.
verses.30:38: Anyone who makes any like it to smell it shall be cut off from his people."
verses.31:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.31:2: "See, I have called Bezalel by name, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,
verses.31:3: and I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, with understanding, with knowledge, and with all craftsmanship,
verses.31:4: to devise designs, to work in gold, in silver, and in bronze,
verses.31:5: and in cutting stone for setting, and in carving wood, to work in all craftsmanship.
verses.31:6: And look, I Myself have appointed with him Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; and into the heart of everyone who is wise of heart I have put wisdom, so that they shall make everything that I have commanded you:
verses.31:7: the tent of meeting, the ark for the testimony, the atonement cover that is over it, and all the furnishings of the tent,
verses.31:8: the table and its utensils, the pure lampstand and all its utensils, the incense altar,
verses.31:9: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, the basin and its stand,
verses.31:10: the finely woven garments, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, the garments of his sons to serve as priests,
verses.31:11: and the anointing oil and the incense of aromatic spices for the holy place; they shall do according to everything that I have commanded you."
verses.31:12: Then the LORD said to Moses,
verses.31:13: "As for you, speak to the sons of Israel, saying, 'Above all, My Sabbaths you shall keep, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you.
verses.31:14: And you shall keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you; whoever profanes it shall certainly be put to death, for anyone who does work on it, that person shall be cut off from the midst of his people.
verses.31:15: Six days work may be done, but on the seventh day is a Sabbath of full rest, holy to the LORD; anyone who does work on the Sabbath day shall certainly be put to death.
verses.31:16: So the sons of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, to observe the Sabbath throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.
verses.31:17: Between Me and the sons of Israel it is a sign forever, for in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed.'"
verses.31:18: Then He gave to Moses, as He finished speaking with him on Mount Sinai, the two tablets of the testimony, stone tablets written with the finger of God.
verses.32:1: The people saw that Moses was slow to come down from the mountain, and the people assembled against Aaron and said to him, "Get up, make for us gods who will go ahead of us; for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt—we do not know what has happened to him."
verses.32:2: Aaron said to them, "Pull off the gold rings that are in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me."
verses.32:3: All the people pulled off from themselves the gold rings that were in their ears and brought them to Aaron.
verses.32:4: He took it from their hand, shaped it with an engraving tool, and made it into a calf of cast metal. Then they said, "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt."
verses.32:5: Aaron saw this and built an altar in front of it; then Aaron proclaimed and said, "Tomorrow is a festival to the LORD."
verses.32:6: So they rose early the next day, offered up burnt offerings, and brought near peace offerings. Then the people sat down to eat and drink, and stood up to revel.
verses.32:7: The LORD spoke to Moses, "Go, descend, for your people, whom you brought up from the land of Egypt, have acted corruptly.
verses.32:8: They have quickly turned aside from the way that I commanded them. They have made for themselves a calf of cast metal, bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and said, 'These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.'
verses.32:10: So now leave Me alone, so that My anger may burn against them and I may consume them; and I will make you into a great nation."
verses.32:11: Then Moses pleaded for the favor of the LORD his God and said, "Why, LORD, should Your anger burn against Your people, whom You brought out from the land of Egypt with great power and with a strong hand?
verses.32:12: Why should the Egyptians say, 'For evil He brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and to consume them off the face of the ground'? Turn back from the burning of Your anger, and relent over the harm against Your people.
verses.32:13: Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, Your servants, to whom You swore by Yourself and spoke to them, 'I will multiply your seed like the stars of the sky, and all this land that I have spoken of I will give to your seed, and they will inherit it forever.'"
verses.32:14: So the LORD relented over the harm that He had spoken of doing to His people.
verses.32:15: Moses turned and descended from the mountain, the two tablets of the testimony in his hand—tablets written on both their sides; on one side and on the other they were written.
verses.32:16: Now the tablets were the handiwork of God, and the writing was the writing of God, incised upon the tablets.
verses.32:17: Joshua heard the sound of the people in their shouting, and he said to Moses, "A sound of battle is in the camp."
verses.32:18: He said, "It is not the sound of crying out in victory, nor the sound of crying out in defeat; a sound of singing is what I hear."
verses.32:19: When he drew near to the camp and saw the calf and the dances, the anger of Moses burned; and he hurled the tablets from his hands and shattered them at the base of the mountain.
verses.32:20: He took the calf that they had made, burned it in the fire, and ground it until it was fine; he scattered it across the face of the water and made the sons of Israel drink it.
verses.32:21: Moses said to Aaron, "What has this people done to you, that you brought a great sin upon them?"
verses.32:22: Aaron said, "Do not let my lord's anger burn; you yourself know the people, that they are given to evil.
verses.32:23: They said to me, 'Make for us gods who will go ahead of us; for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt—we do not know what has happened to him.'
verses.32:24: So I said to them, 'Who has gold?' They pulled it off and gave it to me; and I threw it into the fire, and this calf came out."
verses.32:25: Moses saw the people, that they were unrestrained, for Aaron had let them go unrestrained, to be a mockery among those who rise against them.
verses.32:26: So Moses stood at the gate of the camp and said, "Who is for the LORD? To me!" And all the sons of Levi gathered to him.
verses.32:27: He said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Each of you, put his sword on his thigh, cross through and return from gate to gate in the camp, and kill—each man his brother, each man his friend, and each man his relative.'"
verses.32:28: The sons of Levi did according to the word of Moses, and there fell from the people on that day about three thousand men.
verses.32:29: Moses said, "Consecrate yourselves today for the LORD—for each man was against his son and against his brother—so that He may grant a blessing upon you today."
verses.32:30: On the following day, Moses said to the people, "You yourselves have sinned a great sin. Now I will ascend to the LORD; perhaps I may make atonement on behalf of your sin."
verses.32:31: So Moses returned to the LORD and said, "Please, this people has sinned a great sin, and they have made for themselves gods of gold.
verses.32:32: Now then, if You will forgive their sin—and if not, please erase me from Your book that You have written."
verses.32:33: The LORD said to Moses, "Whoever has sinned against Me, I will erase him from My book.
verses.32:34: Now go, lead the people to the place I spoke of to you. Look, My angel will go ahead of you; yet on the day when I call to account, I will call them to account for their sin."
verses.32:35: And the LORD struck the people because they had made the calf that Aaron made.
verses.33:1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, "Go, ascend from here, you and the people whom you brought up from the land of Egypt, to the land concerning which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, 'To your seed I will give it'—
verses.33:2: and I will send an angel ahead of you, and I will expel the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites—
verses.33:3: to a land flowing with milk and honey. For I will not ascend in your midst, because you are a stiff-necked people, or else I might consume you along the way."
verses.33:4: When the people heard this grim word, they mourned, and not a man put his ornaments upon himself.
verses.33:5: The LORD said to Moses, "Say to the sons of Israel, 'You are a stiff-necked people. Were I to ascend in your midst for a single moment, I would consume you. So now, remove your ornaments from upon you, so that I may know what I will do to you.'"
verses.33:6: So the sons of Israel stripped off their own ornaments, from Mount Horeb on.
verses.33:7: Now Moses would take the tent and pitch it for himself outside the camp, far away from the camp, and he called it the tent of meeting. Whenever anyone was seeking the LORD, he would go out to the tent of meeting that was outside the camp.
verses.33:8: Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would get up and station themselves, each man at the entrance of his tent, and they would look after Moses until he went into the tent.
verses.33:9: And as Moses went into the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the entrance of the tent, and He would speak with Moses.
verses.33:10: All the people would see the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, and all the people would rise and bow down, each man at the entrance of his tent.
verses.33:11: And the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, the way a man speaks to his friend. Afterward he would return to the camp, while his attendant Joshua the son of Nun, a young man, would not depart from within the tent.
verses.33:12: Then Moses said to the LORD, "See, You are saying to me, 'Bring this people up,' yet You have not made known to me whom You will send with me. Still You have said, 'I know you by name, and you have also found favor in My eyes.'
verses.33:13: Now then, if I have indeed found favor in Your eyes, please make Your ways known to me so that I may know You, in order that I may find favor in Your eyes; and see that this nation is Your people."
verses.33:14: He said, "My presence will go, and I will grant you rest."
verses.33:15: Then he said to Him, "If Your presence does not go, do not bring us up from here.
verses.33:16: And by what, then, will it be known that I have found favor in Your eyes, I and Your people? Is it not through Your going with us, so that we are set apart, I and Your people, from every people upon the face of the ground?"
verses.33:17: The LORD said to Moses, "This thing also, which you have spoken, I will do, because you have found favor in My eyes and I know you by name."
verses.33:18: Then he said, "Please let me see Your glory."
verses.33:19: He said, "I Myself will make all My goodness pass before your face, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before you; and I will show favor to whomever I show favor, and I will have compassion on whomever I have compassion."
verses.33:20: Yet He said, "You are not able to see My face, for no human can see Me and live."
verses.33:21: Then the LORD said, "Here is a place beside Me; station yourself upon the rock.
verses.33:22: When My glory is passing by, I will place you in the crevice of the rock, and I will shield you with My palm until I have passed by.
verses.33:23: Then I will remove My palm, and you will see My back; yet My face will not be seen."
verses.34:1: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Carve for yourself two tablets of stone like the first ones, and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you smashed.
verses.34:2: Be prepared for the morning, and go up in the morning to Mount Sinai, and take your stand before Me there on the top of the mountain.
verses.34:3: No one shall go up with you, nor let anyone even be seen anywhere on the mountain; even the flocks and the herds are not to graze opposite that mountain."
verses.34:4: So he carved two tablets of stone like the first ones, and Moses rose early in the morning and went up to Mount Sinai, just as the LORD had commanded him, and took in his hand two tablets of stone.
verses.34:5: Then the LORD came down in the cloud and took His stand with him there, and proclaimed the name of the LORD.
verses.34:6: And the LORD passed in front of him and called out, "The LORD, the LORD, a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, and great in loyal love and faithfulness,
verses.34:7: preserving loyal love for thousands, forgiving iniquity and rebellion and sin; yet He will certainly not acquit the guilty, calling to account the iniquity of fathers upon children and upon children's children, upon the third and upon the fourth generations."
verses.34:8: And Moses hurried and bowed low to the ground and worshiped.
verses.34:9: He said, "If now I have found favor in Your eyes, Lord, let the Lord please walk in our midst, for they are a stiff-necked people, and pardon our iniquity and our sin, and claim us as Your inheritance."
verses.34:10: And He said, "Look, I am making a covenant. In front of all your people I will perform wonders that have not been created in all the earth or among all the nations; and all the people in whose midst you are will see the work of the LORD, for what I am doing with you is awe-inspiring.
verses.34:11: Keep carefully what I am commanding you today. Look, I am driving out from before you the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
verses.34:12: Be on your guard so that you do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land into which you are going, or they will become a snare in your midst.
verses.34:13: Instead, you shall tear down their altars, smash their standing stones, and cut down their Asherah poles,
verses.34:14: for you shall not bow down to another god, because the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God—
verses.34:15: so that you do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and when they prostitute themselves after their gods and sacrifice to their gods, they invite you and you eat from their sacrifice,
verses.34:16: and you take some of their daughters for your sons, and their daughters prostitute themselves after their gods and cause your sons to prostitute themselves after their gods.
verses.34:17: You shall not make cast-metal gods for yourself.
verses.34:18: You shall keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, just as I commanded you, at the appointed time of the month of Abib, because in the month of Abib you went out from Egypt.
verses.34:19: Every first offspring of the womb is Mine, and all your livestock that is male, the first offspring of ox and sheep.
verses.34:20: You shall redeem the first offspring of a donkey with a sheep, and if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck. Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem, and no one shall appear before Me empty-handed.
verses.34:21: For six days you shall labor, but on the seventh day you shall rest; during plowing and during harvest you shall rest.
verses.34:22: And you shall observe for yourself the Feast of Weeks, the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering at the turn of the year.
verses.34:23: Three times each year all your males shall appear before the Sovereign, the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.34:24: For I will dispossess nations from before you and widen your territory, and no one will covet your land when you go up to appear before the LORD your God three times each year.
verses.34:25: You shall not slaughter the blood of My sacrifice with anything leavened, nor shall the sacrifice of the Feast of the Passover remain overnight until the morning.
verses.34:26: The choicest of the firstfruits of your soil you shall bring into the house of the LORD your God. You shall not boil a young goat in the milk of its mother."
verses.34:27: And the LORD said to Moses, "Write for yourself these words, for according to these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."
verses.34:28: And he was there with the LORD for forty days and forty nights; he neither ate bread nor drank water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Words.
verses.34:29: Now it happened as Moses came down from Mount Sinai, with the two tablets of the testimony in the hand of Moses as he came down from the mountain, that Moses did not know that the skin of his face was radiant from his speaking with Him.
verses.34:30: Aaron and all the sons of Israel saw Moses, and look, the skin of his face was radiant, and they were afraid to draw near to him.
verses.34:31: But Moses called out to them, so Aaron and all the leaders in the congregation turned back to him, and Moses spoke to them.
verses.34:32: Afterward all the sons of Israel drew near, and he commanded them everything that the LORD had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.
verses.34:33: And Moses finished speaking with them and placed a veil over his face.
verses.34:34: But whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with Him, he would remove the veil until he came out; and he would come out and speak to the sons of Israel whatever he was commanded.
verses.34:35: And the sons of Israel would see the face of Moses, that the skin of Moses's face was radiant; then Moses would place the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with Him.
verses.35:1: Then Moses assembled the whole congregation of the sons of Israel and said to them, "These are the things that the LORD has commanded to be done:
verses.35:2: For six days work shall be done, but on the seventh day it shall be holy for you, a Sabbath of complete rest to the LORD; everyone who does work on it shall be put to death.
verses.35:3: You shall not light a fire in any of your dwelling places on the Sabbath day."
verses.35:4: And Moses spoke to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, saying, "This is the thing that the LORD has commanded, saying:
verses.35:5: 'Take from among yourselves a contribution for the LORD. Everyone whose heart is willing shall bring it, the contribution for the LORD: gold, silver, and bronze,
verses.35:6: and blue, purple, and crimson yarn, fine linen, and goat hair,
verses.35:7: and ram skins dyed red, skins of fine leather, and acacia wood,
verses.35:9: and onyx stones and stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece.
verses.35:10: And let everyone among you who is skilled of heart come and make everything that the LORD has commanded:
verses.35:11: the tabernacle, its tent and its covering, its clasps and its frames, its crossbars, its pillars, and its bases;
verses.35:12: the ark and its poles, the atonement cover, and the curtain of the screen; and the altar of incense and its poles, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the screen of the entrance for the entrance of the tabernacle; the hangings of the courtyard, its pillars and its bases, and the screen of the gate of the courtyard;
verses.35:13: the table and its poles and all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
verses.35:14: and the lampstand for the light, its utensils, its lamps, and the oil for the light;
verses.35:16: the altar of burnt offering and the bronze grating that belongs to it, its poles and all its utensils, the basin and its stand;
verses.35:19: the finely woven garments for ministering in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for serving as priests.'"
verses.35:20: Then the whole congregation of the sons of Israel went out from before Moses.
verses.35:21: So they came, every person whose heart stirred him and everyone whose spirit made him willing; they brought the contribution for the LORD for the work of the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the holy garments.
verses.35:22: The men came along with the women—all who were willing of heart brought brooches, earrings, signet rings, and pendants, every article of gold—as well as every man who lifted up a wave offering of gold to the LORD.
verses.35:23: And everyone with whom were found blue, purple, and crimson yarn, fine linen, goat hair, ram skins dyed red, and skins of fine leather brought them.
verses.35:24: Everyone offering a contribution of silver and bronze brought the contribution for the LORD, and everyone with whom acacia wood was found for any work of the service brought it.
verses.35:25: And every woman skilled of heart spun with her hands, and they brought spun thread: the blue, the purple, the crimson yarn, and the fine linen.
verses.35:26: And all the women whose heart stirred them with skill spun the goat hair.
verses.35:27: And the leaders brought the onyx stones and the stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece,
verses.35:28: and the spices and the oil for light, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.
verses.35:29: Every man and woman whose heart made them willing to bring anything for all the work that the LORD had commanded by the hand of Moses to be done—the sons of Israel brought a freewill offering to the LORD.
verses.35:30: And Moses said to the sons of Israel, "Look, the LORD has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
verses.35:31: He has filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, with understanding, with knowledge, and with every kind of craftsmanship,
verses.35:32: and to devise designs, to work in gold, in silver, and in bronze,
verses.35:33: and in the cutting of stone for setting, and in the carving of wood, to execute every work of design.
verses.35:34: And He has put it in his heart to teach, both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.
verses.35:35: He has filled them with skill of heart to do every work of a craftsman, of a designer, of an embroiderer in blue, in purple, in crimson yarn, and in fine linen, and of a weaver—makers of every kind of work and devisers of designs."
verses.36:1: So Bezalel and Oholiab, and every wise-hearted man in whom the LORD has placed wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work of the service of the sanctuary, shall work according to everything that the LORD has commanded.
verses.36:2: Then Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab and every wise-hearted man in whose heart the LORD had placed wisdom, everyone whose heart moved him to draw near to the work to do it.
verses.36:3: They received from before Moses the entire contribution that the sons of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary, to do it. Still, they kept bringing to him freewill offerings morning by morning.
verses.36:4: Then all the wise ones who were doing all the work of the sanctuary came, each man from his work that they were doing.
verses.36:5: And they spoke to Moses, saying, "The people are bringing much more than enough for the service of the work that the LORD commanded to be done."
verses.36:6: So Moses gave a command, and they passed a proclamation through the camp, saying, "Let neither man nor woman do any more work for the contribution of the sanctuary." And the people were held back from bringing more.
verses.36:7: For the material was enough for them for all the work, to do it, and to spare.
verses.36:8: From the blue, purple, and crimson yarn they made woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary, and they made the holy garments for Aaron, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.36:9: He made the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and crimson yarn, and twisted fine linen.
verses.36:10: They hammered out thin sheets of gold, and he cut them into threads to work into the blue, into the purple, into the crimson yarn, and into the fine linen, the work of a skilled designer.
verses.36:11: They made attaching shoulder pieces for it; at its two ends it was joined together.
verses.36:12: And the woven band that fastened it, which was on it, was of one piece with it and of the same workmanship: gold, blue, purple, and crimson yarn, and twisted fine linen, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.36:13: They fashioned the onyx stones, enclosed in gold filigree settings, engraved like the engravings of a signet according to the names of the sons of Israel.
